title: fix(i18n/build/ci): ICU-escape 381 message values, externalize tiktoken, add blocking UI-ICU gate
body: ## Summary Three tightly-related fixes, verified live on the latest `release/v3.8.51`: 1. **`fix(i18n)`** — ICU-escape **381 message values** containing raw `` / literal `{...}` across all **42 locale catalogs** (`src/i18n/messages/*.json`). 2. **`fix(build)`** — externalize `tiktoken` in `next.config.mjs` so `tiktoken_bg.wasm` resolves at runtime. 3. **`chore(ci)`** — add a **blocking** `check:ui-icu` gate that compiles every message value with `IntlMessageFormat` (next-intl's parser), so this defect class can never ship again. ## Background A message value containing a raw `` or literal `{...}` fails to compile under `IntlMessageFormat`. At runtime the component silently breaks — the RSC/Flight path throws `INVALID_MESSAGE` and the UI falls back to showing the raw i18n key. This exact class shipped repeatedly: - **#12302** — `ccOnboardingKeyPlaceholder` = `` (crashed the Claude Code onboarding block) - **#12505** — `OMNIROUTE_AUTO_SYNC_CLAUDE_PROFILES.description` = `~/.claude/profiles//settings.json` (Feature Flags page showed the raw key) - **#12559** — `featureFlagExposeFunctionalGatewayMirrorsDescription` = raw `/` - plus literal JSON/regex paste-hint examples (`[{ json, name?, email? }...]`), a service-account JSON placeholder, regex samples, a broken ``/`{` characters must render. HTML entities would corrupt the pasted content. Every single change was asserted **render-identical** (`new IntlMessageFormat(fixed).format() === original`) by `scripts/ad-hoc/fix-invalid-icu.mjs`; the only deliberate wording change is the `nl` `bold"`) and normal ICU (`{count, plural, ...}`) compile fine — no false positives, pinned by `tests/unit/i18n-ui-icu.test.ts` (10 tests). Wired into the blocking `i18n-ui-coverage` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. ## The tiktoken fix (commit 2) `tiktoken` resolves `tiktoken_bg.wasm` at runtime via `fs.readFileSync` relative to `__dirname`; bundled by Turbopack that lookup fails ("Missing tiktoken_bg.wasm") and 500s every route touching codex-chatgpt-web token estimation (e.g. `GET /api/providers`). Externalizing it (like `sqlite-vec` / `better-sqlite3`) keeps the require at runtime. ## Verification - `check:ui-icu` → **PASS — all 545,817 messages in 42 catalogs compile** - `tests/unit/i18n-ui-icu.test.ts` → **10/10 pass** - `check-ui-value-drift` (against base) → **PASS** - `check-ui-keys-coverage` → **PASS** Note: `intl-messageformat` is currently a transitive dep of `next-intl` (^11.1.0) — the gate requires it, so if that dependency is ever dropped it should be promoted to a direct dependency.

title: fix(sse): prefer cgroup PSI for chat admission
body:
## Summary

Chat admission's resource-pressure sampler read host-wide `/proc/pressure/memory`. In Docker that file is the **machine**, not the container: a swapping host 503s idle OmniRoute with `resource_pressure` even when the cgroup is well under its limit (V8/cgroup ratios stay `normal`).

Prefer this unit's cgroup v2 `memory.pressure` when it parses. Keep `/proc/pressure/memory` only as fallback (bare metal, cgroup v1, missing file).

## Test plan

- [x] `node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/resource-pressure-sampler.test.ts`
  - prefers cgroup PSI when both files exist and disagree
  - falls back to `/proc/pressure/memory` when the cgroup pressure file is absent
  - existing sampler cases still pass
- [ ] Docker host under memory PSI, container idle: `/v1/chat/completions` is not 503 `resource_pressure`

title: i18n: 7 new usage.kiloPass* keys missing from 39 locales — Kilo Pass usage meter falls back to English
body:
The Kilo Pass / Kilo Code balance UI (#12178, added 2026-09-01) introduced 7 new strings under `usage.*` in `en.json`, but only **de, pt-BR, vi** have them translated — the other **39 locales** (`ar, az, bg, bn, cs, da, es, fa, fi, fr, gu, he, hi, hu, id, in, it, ja, ko, mr, ms, nl, no, phi, pl, pt, ro, ru, sk, sv, sw, ta, te, th, tr, uk-UA, ur, zh-CN, zh-TW`) are missing all 7 keys and fall back to English (or show raw keys) on the Kilo Pass usage meter.

## Missing keys (en values)
| Key | en value |
|---|---|
| `usage.kiloAccountBalance` | "Account Balance" |
| `usage.kiloPassBonus` | "Available bonus" |
| `usage.kiloPassMeterLabel` | "Kilo Pass usage meter" |
| `usage.kiloPassPaid` | "Paid" |
| `usage.kiloPassRemaining` | "Remaining" |
| `usage.kiloPassRenews` | "Renews {count} days" |
| `usage.kiloPassUsageLabel` | "This month's usage" |

## Also
- `featureFlagOmnirouteDisableThinkingLevelVariantsDescription` is missing **only from `pt.json`** (all other 41 locales have it; `pt-BR` has it).

## How this was found
A full missing/empty/placeholder sweep of all 43 catalogs vs `en.json` (12,951 keys): **274 missing-key occurrences = 8 distinct keys** (the 7 above × 39 locales + the 1 `pt` flag description). Zero empty/null values anywhere. The 1,613 `__MISSING__:` placeholders across 47 other keys are the intentional value-drift escape hatch, not defects.

`de`/`pt-BR`/`vi` are already complete and can serve as reference for the backfill. The existing `check-ui-keys-coverage` gate counts key *presence*, so it won't flag this class until a key is actually deleted — a per-key missing-list would help here, but the immediate ask is just the backfill.

title: i18n: strict ICU compile gate for all 43 locale catalogs (check:ui-icu) — 302 messages shipped that failed to compile
body: Companion to #12302 / #12505 / #12559. A sweep of every message in every locale catalog with `IntlMessageFormat` (the exact parser next-intl uses) found **302 messages across 43 locales that fail to compile** — the same defect class that has now broken pages 4 times (Claude Code onboarding, Feature Flags page ×2, Kilo Pass labels). next-intl silently swallows these failures at runtime (`createTranslator` does not surface them), so every one of these pages was quietly falling back to raw key names. ## Proposal: a blocking CI gate that compiles all 556,619 messages `scripts/i18n/check-ui-icu.mjs` (168 lines): - Compiles **every message value** in `src/i18n/messages/*.json` (43 catalogs, 556,619 messages, ~6s) with `IntlMessageFormat`. - Any compile error (`INVALID_TAG`, `UNCLOSED_TAG`, `MALFORMED_ARGUMENT`, …) exits 1 → PR fails. - `--warn` / `--json` flags, exported pure helpers (`findInvalidMessages`, `flattenLeaves`), matching the conventions of `check-ui-value-drift.mjs`. - Unit-tested: `tests/unit/i18n-ui-icu.test.ts` (10 cases — both known bug classes throw, legit `t.rich` rich-text compiles, escaped values pass, no false positives). - Wired into the blocking `i18n-ui-coverage` job in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` via `npm run check:ui-icu` (added to `package.json`). Legitimate rich-text (`"bold"` used with `t.rich`) and normal ICU (`{count, plural, ...}`) compile fine — no false positives. ## The 302 failures it would have caught (all fixed locally, render-identical) `scripts/ad-hoc/fix-invalid-icu.mjs` applied per-key transforms and **asserted `format(fixed) === original` for every single change** — every fix is provably render-identical. Breakdown: 1. **Raw `` in plain-`t()` messages** (live bugs, same class as the filed issues): - `featureFlagExposeFunctionalGatewayMirrorsDescription` = `Advertise / mirror ids...` — 43 locales (filed as #12559) - `ccOnboardingKeyPlaceholder` = `` — 43 locales (filed as #12302) - `OMNIROUTE_AUTO_SYNC_CLAUDE_PROFILES.description` = `~/.claude/profiles//settings.json` — 43 locales (filed as #12505) 2. **Literal JSON/regex paste-hint examples** with raw `{...}` braces (e.g. `[{ json, name?, email? }...]` schema hints) that render as raw text but fail strict ICU parsing — wrapped the literal braces in ICU quotes (render-identical). 3. **`{" "}` artifacts** in `phi`/`sv` status labels (`pinned`/`lastUsed`) — quoted fragment. 4. **Broken rich-text tag** in Dutch (`deze`) — corrected to a matching tag. Result: **all 556,619 messages in all 43 catalogs now compile cleanly.** ## Verified - `npm run check:ui-icu` → PASS (0 failures) - `check-ui-value-drift` (existing blocking gate) → PASS — the 2 locales whose English changed (`vi`, `pt-BR`) were refreshed to track it - `check-ui-keys-coverage` → PASS - `tests/unit/i18n-ui-icu.test.ts` → 10/10 - Locale diff is surgical (390/390 lines across 43 files, no reformat noise) ## Notes - `intl-messageformat` is currently a **transitive** dep of `next-intl` (^11.1.0) — the gate requires it; if upstream ever drops that dependency, promote it to a direct dependency. - Suggested follow-up: apply the same strict compile check to the CLI i18n catalogs (`scripts/check/check-cli-i18n.mjs` covers keys but not ICU validity).

title: i18n: raw `<gateway-alias>`/`<model>` tag in featureFlagExposeFunctionalGatewayMirrorsDescription (all 43 locales) breaks the Feature Flags page
body:
Same defect class as #12302 and #12505: a message value with a raw `<tag>` that is rendered through plain `t()` (not `t.rich`) fails ICU compilation under next-intl and silently breaks the page — the card falls back to showing the raw key name instead of the description.

## Environment
- Branch: `release/v3.8.51` @ `073b98462` (latest, fully synced)
- Reported from a fork; Windows 11, Node 24, dev mode

## Symptom
The `OMNIROUTE_EXPOSE_FUNCTIONAL_GATEWAY_MIRRORS` flag card on `/dashboard/settings/feature-flags` renders the raw key name instead of the description, and the browser console logs `INVALID_MESSAGE: INVALID_TAG`.

## Root cause
All 43 locale catalogs (`src/i18n/messages/*.json`) contain:

```json
"featureFlagExposeFunctionalGatewayMirrorsDescription": "Advertise <gateway-alias>/<model> mirror ids on /v1/models ..."
```

The Feature Flags grid renders flag descriptions via **plain `t()`**:

- `src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/settings/components/FeatureFlagsGrid.tsx:140`
  `matchesSearch(t(`definitions.${f.key}.description`), debouncedSearch)`

next-intl parses `<gateway-alias>` and `<model>` as unknown rich-text tags with no matching element → the message fails to compile → `t()` falls back to the key name.

`featureFlagDefinitions.ts:540` wires the key (`descriptionI18nKey`).

## Verified fix (already applied locally, all 43 files)
Wrap the literal tags in **ICU single quotes** — renders identical text but compiles:

```
"description": "Advertise '<gateway-alias>'/'<model>' mirror ids on /v1/models ..."
```

Verified two ways:
1. `IntlMessageFormat` (next-intl's parser): `Advertise '<gateway-alias>'/'<model>' mirror ids...` → renders exactly `Advertise <gateway-alias>/<model> mirror ids...` with no error.
2. Live page: the flag card now shows the full description; console clean.

## Why not `<`/`>`
The value is a human-readable explanation of mirror-id syntax — the literal angle brackets must render (`<gateway-alias>/<model>` is an id pattern users see). HTML entities would display incorrectly.

## Notes
- This was the 4th live instance of this bug class: #12302 (`ccOnboardingKeyPlaceholder`), #12505 (`OMNIROUTE_AUTO_SYNC_CLAUDE_PROFILES.description`), and the `{" "}` artifacts in `phi`/`sv`. A strict ICU compile gate for all catalogs (`npm run check:ui-icu`, wired into CI) now exists to prevent regressions — see the companion issue.

title: feat(sse): add dynamic claude code client version and identity resolver
body:
## Summary
Resolves hardcoded Claude Code client version and fingerprint drift by introducing a dynamic identity resolver.

### Problem
Previously, `CLAUDE_CODE_CLIENT_VERSION` and associated metadata were static constants. When upstream Anthropic/Claude Code releases new client versions or requires updated wire identities for newly released models, static constants lead to outdated headers, fingerprint divergence, or upstream rejections.

### Solution
1. **Dynamic Identity Resolver (`src/shared/services/claudeCodeIdentity.ts`)**:
   - Resolves consistent `ClaudeCodeIdentity` tuple (`version`, `buildRevision`, `sdkVersion`, `runtimeVersion`, `billingVersion`, `userAgentCli`, `userAgentSdkCli`).
   - Priority pipeline:
     - Explicit environment override (`CLAUDE_CODE_CLIENT_VERSION` or `CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION_MODE=fixed`)
     - Locally installed binary (`claude --version` via `execFile` without shell interpolation)
     - NPM registry lookup (`@anthropic-ai/claude-code` dist-tags with configurable channel `stable` or `latest`)
     - Bundled known-good baseline fallback (`2.1.236`)
   - In-memory SWR caching so hot-path calls (`getClaudeCodeIdentity()`) have zero latency.
2. **Unified Facade (`src/shared/constants/claudeCodeClient.ts`)**:
   - Dynamic accessors while maintaining backward-compatible constant exports.
3. **Synchronized Downstream Consumers**:
   - Updated `open-sse/config/anthropicHeaders.ts`, `open-sse/config/providers/shared.ts`, `open-sse/executors/base.ts`, `open-sse/services/claudeCodeCompatible.ts`, and `open-sse/services/ccBridgeTransforms.ts`.
   - Async bootstrap initialization in `src/instrumentation-node.ts`.
4. **Environment Variables**:
   - Added `CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION_MODE`, `CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION_CHANNEL`, `CLAUDE_CODE_CLIENT_VERSION`, `CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION_CACHE_TTL` to `.env.example`.

### Testing
- Added unit test suite `tests/unit/claude-code-dynamic-identity.test.ts`.
- Verified lockstep synchronization in `tests/unit/claude-codex-identity-version-sync.test.ts`.
- Passed all unit tests, TypeScript typecheck (`npm run typecheck:core`), and cycles check (`npm run check:cycles`).

title: chore(electron): drop openAsHidden/wasOpenedAsHidden, removed in Electron 44
body:
Follow-up to #12217 (electron 43.4.1 → 44.0.0).

Electron 44 removed `openAsHidden` from `app.setLoginItemSettings()` and `wasOpenedAsHidden` from `app.getLoginItemSettings()`. Both were still referenced here — `electron/main.js` passed `openAsHidden: true` when enabling autostart, and `shouldStartHidden()` treated `loginItemSettings.wasOpenedAsHidden === true` as a hidden launch.

**Nothing regressed when #12217 landed, and nothing changes now.** The live hidden-autostart path is `args: ["--hidden"]`, registered with the login item and matched by the `argv.includes("--hidden")` check that `shouldStartHidden()` evaluates first; Linux never reaches that API at all (it goes through `enableLinuxDesktopAutostart`). `openAsHidden` only ever worked on macOS 12 and below — exactly the versions Electron 44 drops. This PR removes the dead second path so the code stops describing a mechanism the runtime no longer has.

`shouldStartHidden()` also loses its `loginItemSettings` parameter, which lets the startup sequence skip an `app.getLoginItemSettings()` call made solely to read a field that is now always `undefined`.

### Validation

- `tests/unit/electron-lazy-window.test.ts` updated to pin the new contract in both directions: login-item settings are ignored *even when they still carry* `wasOpenedAsHidden: true` (guards against re-introducing the dependency), and `main.js` must keep registering the `--hidden` argument while never mentioning `openAsHidden`. 8/8 pass.
- All 16 `tests/unit/electron-*.test.ts` files: **165/165 pass**.

Also adds the CHANGELOG fragment recording the user-facing consequence of #12217: the desktop app now requires macOS 13 (Ventura) or later.

title: docs(reference): sync FEATURE_FLAGS.md with featureFlagDefinitions
body:
## Summary

- `docs/reference/FEATURE_FLAGS.md:10-13` promises that its catalog is "generated to match [`featureFlagDefinitions.ts`] 1:1", but on `release/v3.8.51` it had drifted: 20 of the 54 keys in `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS` (`src/shared/constants/featureFlagDefinitions.ts:14-655`) had no row (3 security, 2 network, 2 policies, 11 runtime, 2 cli), two rows were not flags at all (`INPUT_SANITIZER_BLOCK_THRESHOLD` and its legacy alias `INJECTION_GUARD_BLOCK_THRESHOLD` are plain env vars read in `src/shared/utils/injectionSeverity.ts:48-49`, with no DB override or dashboard toggle), the summary line said 37 flags and the `GET` example said "all 33 flags" / `"total": 33`, the per-category headings were stale (7/8/3/11/3/3 vs 10/9/5/22/5/3), and the `OMNIROUTE_ENABLE_LIVE_WS` row named port 20129 while the code default is 20132 (`src/app/api/v1/ws/route.ts:30`, `src/server/ws/liveServer.ts:4`).
- The six catalog tables are regenerated from the definitions (category, type, default, `requiresRestart`), in definition order. Rows that already existed keep their curated wording; the 20 new rows use the definition's `description` (plus the `Values:` list for the two enums). The two threshold env vars move to a note under the tables that points at `ENVIRONMENT.md`, where they are already documented. Counts, the JSON example, and the frontmatter are refreshed. No values of previously documented rows changed (the static check found zero type/default mismatches on the base).
- Guard: `tests/unit/feature-flags-doc-sync-static.test.ts` parses the catalog and asserts, against `FEATURE_FLAG_DEFINITIONS`, that every defined flag has a row, every row is a defined flag, category/type/default/restart match, and the heading counts and the "N flags across M categories" total match. Red on the base (3 of 4 fail), green here.
- `scripts/check/check-fabricated-docs.mjs` (strict in `quality.yml`) would have failed on six of the new rows with "env var is never read", because `resolveFeatureFlag()` reads `process.env[definition.key]` dynamically (`src/shared/utils/featureFlags.ts:45`) and the literal scan cannot see it. The checker now reads every `key:` in `featureFlagDefinitions.ts` into its documented-env-var index; this generalizes the existing one-off `MODELS_CATALOG_PREFIX_MODE` allowlist entry, which is removed. Its own suite (`tests/unit/check-fabricated-docs.test.ts`, 25/25) and the strict run stay green. No production code changes.

## Related Issues

- No open issue tracks this drift (`gh issue list --search "FEATURE_FLAGS"` returns nothing relevant).
- Related to #12486, which adds `REASONING_REPLAY_ENABLED` to `featureFlagDefinitions.ts`; once it lands the new static test will ask for its row (one line in the Runtime table).

## Validation

- [x] Change type: other (documentation + doc-accuracy checker + static test)
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path: `tests/unit/feature-flags-doc-sync-static.test.ts` 4/4, `tests/unit/check-fabricated-docs.test.ts` 25/25, `npm run check:fabricated-docs` (strict) OK, `npm run check:docs-sync` PASS, `npm run check:docs-counts` OK, `node scripts/check/check-doc-links.mjs` PASS (955 links), `npm run check:changelog-integrity` OK
- [ ] `npm run lint` — not run repository-wide; `eslint` and `prettier --check` on the touched files exit 0 (`scripts/check/*.mjs` is eslint-ignored by the repo config; prettier applied)
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base `release/v3.8.51`; focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR (no `src/` change; the doc gets a static test)
- SonarQube is temporarily opt-in while the private project has no quota; it is not a PR gate.

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/feature-flags-doc-sync-static.test.ts` (new, 4 cases): defined flags all present; no undefined rows; category/type/default/restart parity; heading and total counts. On the base doc: `not ok 1`, `not ok 2`, `ok 3`, `not ok 4`. With this change: 4/4.
- No production code changed. `tests/unit/check-fabricated-docs.test.ts` is unchanged and green; its case "real documentation has no fabricated claims" is the one that would have caught the six dynamically resolved flags without the checker change.

## Coverage Notes

- No `src/`, `open-sse/`, `electron/`, or `bin/` files changed. The checker change is exercised by `tests/unit/check-fabricated-docs.test.ts` (which calls `buildCodebaseIndex` on the real repo) and by the strict run.

## Reviewer Notes

- Descriptions for the 20 new rows are taken verbatim from `featureFlagDefinitions.ts`; the test deliberately does not compare descriptions, so the doc can keep curated wording (cross-links, `**Danger.**`) without churn.
- `OMNIROUTE_ENABLE_LIVE_WS`: only the port number in the description changed (20129 -> 20132). If 20129 is meant somewhere, it is not the default in `src/app/api/v1/ws/route.ts`.
- Removing `MODELS_CATALOG_PREFIX_MODE` from `ENV_VAR_ALLOWLIST` is safe because the same key is now supplied by the definitions file; if the flag is ever deleted from the code, the docs that mention it (`API_REFERENCE.md`, `VSCODE-COPILOT.md`) start failing the strict check, which is the desired behavior.
- Open PRs touching the same files: #12534 also edits `scripts/check/check-fabricated-docs.mjs` (allowlist area; trivial to rebase either way); #12486 and #12549 edit `featureFlagDefinitions.ts` (not touched here). Nothing else open touches `FEATURE_FLAGS.md`.
- The changelog fragment is named `PENDING-…`; rename to the PR number on open.

title: fix(i18n): translate the home Recent Requests panel and topology legend
body:
## Summary

- On a non-English dashboard the home page mixed languages in the two live widgets. The "Recent Requests" panel (`src/app/(dashboard)/home/HomeRecentRequests.tsx`) already reads every label through `useTranslations("home")`, but the five keys it uses (`home.recentRequests`, `recentRequestsEmpty`, `recentRequestsModel`, `recentRequestsTokens`, `recentRequestsWhen`) shipped in #10900 as verbatim English copies in 39 of the 41 non-English catalogs (only pt-BR and vi were translated). A verbatim copy is invisible to every i18n gate: `check-ui-keys-coverage` counts it as covered, `sync-ui-keys` only backfills absent keys, and `check-ui-value-drift` only sees English values that change. So the panel rendered "RECENT REQUESTS / Model / In / Out / When" in es, fr, de, it, ja and every other locale.
- The Provider Topology legend (`src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/HomeProviderTopologySection.tsx`) borrowed three labels from unrelated namespaces: `common.active`, `settings.recent` (the memory-retrieval "Chronological window" toggle, itself an English copy in 33 locales) and `analytics.modelStatusError` (lower-case "error" in es). The result in Spanish was "Activo · Recent · error" under a Spanish title.
- Fix: the legend now owns its three labels, `home.topologyLegendActive` / `topologyLegendRecent` / `topologyLegendError`, next to the `home.activeError` subtitle they sit under, with consistent capitalisation per locale. The recent-requests keys get real translations in es, pt, fr, de and it (pt-BR and vi were already correct); the legend keys are translated in es, pt, pt-BR, fr, de, it and vi. Every other locale gets the repo's `__MISSING__:<english>` marker (the form #12401 used for new keys) instead of a silent English copy — the runtime still falls back to English there, but the keys are now visible to `i18n:sync-ui --translate-markers`. Where a locale already had a translated `common.active` / `settings.recent` / `analytics.modelStatusError`, that translation is reused for the legend rather than a marker (54 reused, 48 markers across the 34 locales I did not translate by hand). No English value changed, so the value-drift gate is unaffected.
- Deliberately out of scope (same root cause, different surface, kept for a follow-up so this PR stays one defect): the `FirstRunReadinessCard` `home.readiness*` keys (10) plus `home.stepError`, `home.requestsShort`, `home.aliasLabel` are also English copies in es and most locales; `analytics.modelStatusError` is still lower-case "error" in es on the analytics page; `settings.recent` remains an English copy in 33 locales on the memory settings tab.

## Before / after (es-ES)

Before:

```
RECENT REQUESTS                     Topología del proveedor
Model      In / Out      When        0 activo · 1 error     ● Activo  ● Recent  ● error
No requests yet.
```

After:

```
SOLICITUDES RECIENTES               Topología del proveedor
Modelo     Entrada / Salida  Cuándo  0 activo · 1 error     ● Activo  ● Reciente  ● Error
Aún no hay solicitudes.
```

## Related Issues

- No open issue covers this (`gh issue list --search "recent requests i18n"` / `--search topology` return unrelated backlog items).

## Validation

- [x] Change type: i18n / UI
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path: `tests/unit/i18n-home-recent-requests-topology-legend.test.ts` 5/5; neighbouring i18n suites (`i18n-vi-completeness`, `i18n-placeholder-parity`, `i18n-ui-value-drift`, `i18n-pt-br`, `i18n-locale-surfaces-parity`, `translator-friendly-i18n-keys`, `i18n-hardcoded-ui-regressions`, `i18n-translation-ratio-gate`, `i18n-config`) 250/250; `npm run i18n:check-ui-coverage` PASS (41 locales ≥ 80%); `BASE_REF=origin/release/v3.8.51 npm run i18n:check-value-drift` PASS; `npm run i18n:check-ratio` OK (41 locales within baseline +0.5); `npm run check:changelog-integrity` OK; `node scripts/check/check-complexity-ratchets.mjs --base-ref origin/release/v3.8.51` OK (0 violations)
- [ ] `npm run lint` — not run repository-wide; eslint and prettier were run on the two touched TS files and the catalogs, both clean
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base `release/v3.8.51`; focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR
- SonarQube is temporarily opt-in while the private project has no quota; it is not a PR gate.

Red on the base: the new test file fails 4 of 5 cases against `release/v3.8.51` (keys missing, English copies present, legend borrowing `settings.recent`); green with this change (5/5).

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/i18n-home-recent-requests-topology-legend.test.ts` (new, 5 cases): the eight home-widget keys exist and are non-empty in all 42 catalogs; es/pt/pt-BR/fr/de/it/vi hold real translations (no `__MISSING__` marker, not the English value, with `es.home.topologyLegendError = "Error"` allow-listed as a genuine cognate); no locale keeps a silent English copy of the five recent-requests keys (translated or marked); `HomeProviderTopologySection.tsx` reads the legend from `home.topologyLegend*` and no longer from `settings.recent` / `analytics.modelStatusError`; the three legend labels share capitalisation within each maintained locale.

## Coverage Notes

- `src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/HomeProviderTopologySection.tsx`: the only production change is three `t()` calls and the removal of three unused `useTranslations` hooks; the new static test pins the key names it must use. No touched file lost coverage.
- `src/i18n/messages/*.json`: catalog data, covered by the new test and the existing i18n gates listed above.

## Reviewer Notes

- The `__MISSING__:` markers replace values that were already English, so nothing regresses visually in those locales: `deepMergeFallback` (`src/i18n/request.ts`) renders the English fallback exactly as before. The change makes the debt visible to the translation pipeline instead of hiding it as "covered".
- `nl.home.recentRequestsModel` becomes `__MISSING__:Model` although Dutch "Model" is correct; I left it to the pipeline rather than hand-pick cognates outside the languages I can vouch for. The same applies to any other coincidental cognate among the marked locales.
- German legend "Zuletzt" (most recently routed) was chosen over "Kürzlich" because the amber dot marks the last provider that served a request, not a time window.
- Manual check on a Spanish UI: home page with `showProviderTopologyOnHome` enabled, then confirm the panel header, the three column headers, the empty state and the legend all read in Spanish, and that the legend casing matches the "Activo · Reciente · Error" row.

title: fix(orchestration): emit the real task status on non-status updates
body:
## Summary

- `updateCloudAgentTask` (`src/lib/cloudAgent/db.ts:124`) published `state: "updated"` on `agent.task.updated` whenever the update carried no `status` field. The `activities` sync in `src/app/api/v1/agents/tasks/[id]/route.ts:175` and the `result`/`error` writes hit that path, so the `agents` WS channel carried a fabricated state that no `OrchState` maps to. This is the first bullet of the PR-B1 minors in #12392 ("read the row's real `status` or document `"updated"` as a sentinel").
- The writer now reads the row's current `status` after the `UPDATE` and publishes that; a status-carrying update still publishes the value it wrote, without the extra read. When no row matched the id nothing was written, so nothing is published either (the A2A `updateTask` already behaves this way for an unknown id).
- Deliberately out of scope: the duplicated `emitAgentTaskUpdated` helper (third bullet, it needs `a2a/taskManager.ts` and lands better after PR-B2), the no-op `status` write in the GET sync (fourth bullet), and the `hubProxy` module-level state (second bullet).

## Related Issues

title: fix(i18n): quote raw <name> in the auto-sync profiles description
body:
## Summary

- `featureFlags.definitions.OMNIROUTE_AUTO_SYNC_CLAUDE_PROFILES.description` (`src/i18n/messages/en.json:12971` and the same key in the other 41 locales) carries the literal path `~/.claude/profiles/<name>/settings.json`. next-intl parses `<name>` as a rich-text tag; `FeatureFlagsGrid.tsx:426-428` renders the description through plain `t()` and never passes a tag element, so the message fails to compile with `INVALID_MESSAGE: UNCLOSED_TAG` and the Settings → Feature Flags card shows the raw key instead of the description, in every language.
- The placeholder is now wrapped in ICU single quotes (`'<name>'`) in all 42 locale files and in the TypeScript default (`src/shared/constants/featureFlagDefinitions.ts:613`), the same form as #12369 for `ccOnboardingKeyPlaceholder`. One substring changed per file, nothing else touched. Reproduced and verified against `use-intl`'s `development` build (the one Turbopack dev mode loads): raw `<name>` → `UNCLOSED_TAG` + key fallback; `'<name>'` → the literal path renders; `<name>` → the entities are returned verbatim by `t()` and would be displayed as text, so the entity form used by earlier fixes is not suitable for a real file path the user is meant to copy. The production build of `use-intl` tolerates the raw tag on the plain `t()` path, which is why the symptom is context-dependent, as the report says.
- Deliberately out of scope: the reporter's second follow-up (a CI gate that parses every `en.json` value with the ICU parser). `tests/unit/i18n-vi-completeness.test.ts` already skips any key whose English source does not parse, so that gate is a separate change with its own allowlist; it will be proposed as an issue first. This PR fixes one message and adds one focused guard.

## Related Issues

- Closes #12505
- Related to #12302 / #12369 (same class, `ccOnboardingKeyPlaceholder`, same ICU-quote form)

## Validation

- [x] Change type: i18n
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path: new test 5/5; `tests/unit/i18n-vi-completeness.test.ts`, `i18n-cc-alias-unclosed-tags`, `i18n-deno-relay-unclosed-tag`, `i18n-placeholder-parity`, `i18n-ui-value-drift`, `i18n-translation-ratio-gate`, `settings-i18n-keys`, `i18n-config` 43/43; `npm run i18n:sync-ui:dry`, `npm run i18n:check-ui-coverage`, `npm run i18n:check-value-drift`, `npm run i18n:check-glossary` all PASS; `npm run check:changelog-integrity` OK; `node scripts/check/check-complexity-ratchets.mjs --base-ref origin/release/v3.8.51` OK; `vi.json` carries no `__MISSING__` marker for this key

title: fix(db): auto-clean conversation_turn_nodes and orphaned conversations
body:
## Summary

- `conversation_turn_nodes` and `agentic_conversations` (migrations 155/156, #10263) had no retention path at all: `src/lib/db/cleanup.ts` never referenced either table, there is no cascade FK, and nothing else deletes from them. The reporter's numbers in #12453 (1.15M node rows, ~775 MB of a 1.1 GB `storage.sqlite` after four days, ~190 MB/day) are the same failure class as #6848 / #4354 / #10421.
- The nodes are identity-only: the transcript view resolves each turn's display content from the `call_logs` row that `last_correlation_id` points at (`156_conversation_turn_nodes.sql` header). Once `cleanupCallLogs` purges that row the node can never render again, so both tables now follow the existing `retention.callLogs` window (`src/types/databaseSettings.ts`) instead of getting a knob of their own, as the issue proposes. No new dashboard setting, no new environment variable, and `docs/reference/ENVIRONMENT.md` is untouched because there is nothing new to document there.
- Two new functions registered at the end of `runAutoCleanup`: `cleanupConversationTurnNodes()` deletes nodes with `last_seen_at` before the cutoff through the shared `deleteFromTableBefore` helper (`src/lib/db/cleanup/usagePurge.ts`, so a database that predates migration 156 is a no-op rather than an error); `cleanupAgenticConversations()` then sweeps roots past the same cutoff that have no remaining node, with `WHERE last_seen_at < ? AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM conversation_turn_nodes n WHERE n.conversation_id = agentic_conversations.id)`. The `last_seen_at` guard uses the index from migration 155 and keeps a root that `createConversation` wrote moments ago, before the same request inserted its nodes.
- Semantics are the ones the issue describes: deleting an old node only affects reconnect anchors, and a conversation resumed after the window mints a new id, which is already the documented anchor-miss behavior of `resolveConversationId`. Deliberately out of scope: the "Clear all" / `resetUsageHistory` paths (a separate, user-triggered contract), and a `last_seen_at` index on `conversation_turn_nodes`. The node DELETE is a table scan today because migration 156 defined no index on that column; it runs once per cleanup cycle, and I can send the index as a follow-up migration if the maintainer wants it.

## Related Issues

- Closes #12453
- Related to #10263
- Related to #6848

## Validation

- [x] Change type: DB (auto-cleanup lifecycle)
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path: `tests/unit/db-cleanup-conversation-nodes-12453.test.ts` + `telemetry-auto-cleanup-6848` + `db-cleanup` + `db-cleanup-xp-audit-log` 23/23, `npm run check:db-rules` OK, `node scripts/check/check-complexity-ratchets.mjs --base-ref origin/release/v3.8.51` OK (0 violations), `npm run check:changelog-integrity` OK, `npm run typecheck:core` 0 errors
- [ ] `npm run lint`
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base `release/v3.8.51`; focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR
- SonarQube is temporarily opt-in while the private project has no quota; it is not a PR gate.

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/db-cleanup-conversation-nodes-12453.test.ts` (new, 4 cases, real SQLite adapter in a `mkdtemp` `DATA_DIR`, same pattern as `telemetry-auto-cleanup-6848.test.ts`): nodes older than `retention.callLogs` deleted and recent ones kept; stale orphan root swept while a stale-but-anchored root and a fresh root without nodes both stay; a chain whose nodes expire is swept in the same pass, and never before its nodes are gone; `runAutoCleanup` reports `conversationTurnNodes` and `agenticConversations` with the expected counts. Red on the base (4/4 fail: `cleanupConversationTurnNodes is not a function`, `cleanupAgenticConversations is not a function`, `conversationTurnNodes missing from results`), green with the change (4/4).

## Coverage Notes

- `src/lib/db/cleanup.ts`: `cleanupConversationTurnNodes`, `cleanupAgenticConversations` and their registration in `runAutoCleanup` are exercised end-to-end by the new test file; the existing `tests/unit/db-cleanup.test.ts` and `telemetry-auto-cleanup-6848.test.ts` stay green.
- No touched file lost coverage.

## Reviewer Notes

- Purely additive in `cleanup.ts`: two new functions inserted before `runAutoCleanup` and two new entries at the end of its `results` map. #10409 also edits this file, but in different hunks (`cleanupMcpAudit`, `cleanupA2aEvents`, `resetUsageHistory`), so the two should merge cleanly in either order. #12448 edits `src/lib/db/agenticConversations.ts`, which this PR does not touch.
- Behavior change for operators: with the default `retention.callLogs` (30 days), conversations idle for longer than that lose their reconnect anchor and start a new conversation id on resume. Operators who set a short call-log retention (the reporter runs 3 days) get the same window for anchors, which is the trade-off the issue asks for.
- The node DELETE scans `conversation_turn_nodes` (no `last_seen_at` index in migration 156). On the reporter's 1.15M-row table that is one pass per cleanup cycle; if that is a concern I will add the index as a follow-up migration rather than widen this PR.

title: fix(images): /v1/images/edits flattens a combo to its first target and never falls back
body:
### Problem / Use Case `/v1/images/edits` accepts a combo name, but it flattens the combo to its first target and never tries the others, while `/v1/images/generations` runs the full combo strategy with per-target fallback since #9239. The same combo therefore behaves differently on the two image routes. Where it happens on `release/v3.8.51`: - `resolveSingleImageComboTarget()` (`src/lib/images/imageRouteModel.ts:60-75`) returns only the first target that has a `modelStr`; `resolveImageRouteModel()` uses it for every bare (slash-less) name at `:91-96`. - `src/app/api/v1/images/edits/route.ts:346-365` calls `resolveImageRouteModel(fullModel)` once and continues with a single `resolvedModel`. There is no `getComboByName` / `executeImageCombo` diversion in that file; the one in `generations/route.ts:155-163` runs *before* `resolveImageRouteModel` precisely "so we skip single-target flattening" (comment at `:156`). - The edit-capable branches are `codex-responses` (`edits/route.ts:395`), `fal-ai` edit models (`:484`), `adobe-firefly-image` (`:532`), `openrouter` (`:551`) and custom OpenAI-compatible nodes (`:605+`). Anything else with a built-in config gets `400 Image edit is not supported for built-in provider "

"` at `:597-603`; a built-in with no credentials gets `401 No credentials for provider` at `:414-419`; a custom node with none gets `400` at `:623-628`; rate limits return `429` at `:420` / `:629`. Concrete case — combo `img-edit` with targets `[openai/gpt-image-2, codex/gpt-image-2]` or `[adobe-firefly/firefly-image-4, codex/gpt-image-2]`, Codex credentials present: - `POST /v1/images/generations {"model":"img-edit"}` → `executeImageCombo` filters image-capable targets, iterates them, skips the ones without credentials or rate-limited (`open-sse/services/imageCombo.ts:98-122`), returns the first success with `fallbackAttempts` in the meta headers. - `POST /v1/images/edits` with `model=img-edit` → resolves to the first target and answers `400 Image edit is not supported for built-in provider "openai"` (or `401 No credentials for provider: adobe-firefly` when Firefly is first and not connected). The second target could have served the edit and is never consulted. The combo's order also matters more than it should: a user who lists a generation-only provider first gets a hard 400 on edits even though the combo is perfectly valid for generations. ### Proposed Solution Give `/v1/images/edits` the same combo semantics as generations, in two steps so the first is a pure refactor: 1. Extract the target loop of `executeImageCombo()` (`imageCombo.ts:83-156`: credential resolution, `allRateLimited` skip, terminal-vs-retryable classification, fallback count) into a generic `runImageComboTargets(targets, { filter, dispatch })` and have `executeImageCombo` call it with `handleImageGeneration` as the dispatch. No behaviour change on generations. 2. In `edits/route.ts`, when the model is a bare combo name, run the same loop with an edit-capable filter (Codex, Firefly, Fal edit models, OpenRouter, custom OpenAI-compatible nodes) and a dispatch that reuses the route's existing per-provider branches; keep the terminal statuses (400/401/403) terminal per target so a combo with no edit-capable target still answers clearly, and surface `fallbackAttempts` in the meta headers as generations does. Open points I would like your call on before writing it: - Whether a target that answers 401 (no credentials) should be skipped like on generations (`imageCombo.ts:109-113` treats missing credentials as retryable) or stay terminal as the edits route does today. - Whether the combo diversion should also apply to `n > 1` / multi-reference requests, or only to the single-image path first. ### Alternatives Considered - Only re-ordering the combo in the dashboard: works for one user, but any combo that mixes generation-only and edit-capable providers stays order-sensitive on edits and not on generations. - Making `resolveSingleImageComboTarget` prefer an edit-capable target when called from the edits route: fixes the 400 but still gives up on the first credential/rate-limit failure, so it is half of the generations behaviour. - Having the edits route call `executeImageCombo` directly: not possible today, it dispatches `handleImageGeneration` and does not carry the multipart image bytes, hence the generic runner in step 1. ### Acceptance Criteria - `POST /v1/images/edits` with a bare combo name whose first target is not edit-capable, and whose later target is, returns the later target's result with `fallbackAttempts >= 1`. - A combo with no edit-capable target returns one 400 that names the combo, not the first provider. - Rate-limited (429) and 5xx targets fall through to the next target; the last error is returned when all fail, as on generations. - `/v1/images/generations` combo behaviour and `tests/unit/combo/image-combo.test.ts` are unchanged by step 1. ### Area Proxy / Routing, Provider Support ### Related Provider(s) Codex, Adobe Firefly, Fal, OpenRouter, OpenAI-compatible custom providers ### Additional Context Combo/alias resolution on both routes: #3214 / #3215 (PR #3219), bare combos over aliases: #3527. Full combo strategy on generations only: #9239 (PR #9499; `open-sse/services/imageCombo.ts`, `src/app/api/v1/images/generations/route.ts`). Response shape fix that touched both routes: #12268 / PR #12362. Base `release/v3.8.51`, commit `1a0375f`. ### Expected Test Plan - Extend `tests/unit/image-routes-combo-edits-3214-3215.test.ts` (the file #9239's test plan pointed at for multi-target combos) with: first target generation-only + second Codex → 200 from Codex; first target without credentials + second with → 200; no edit-capable target → single 400; all rate-limited → 429. - Keep `tests/unit/combo/image-combo.test.ts` green after the extraction, plus `image-generation-route`, `8510-adobe-firefly-edits-route`, `10197-openrouter-image-edits-route`, `fal-image-edit`; `typecheck:core`, `check:open-sse-typecheck`, `check-complexity-ratchets`. Happy to send the two PRs (refactor first, then the edits wiring) once you have picked the 401 semantics.

title: fix(gamification): action_count badges are computed over a 30-day-pruned xp_audit_log
body:
### Problem / Use Case

The four `request` action-count badges are computed over a table that is pruned every 30 days by default, so the lifetime totals they describe can never be reached on a default install.

`checkActionCountBadges()` (`src/lib/gamification/events.ts:171-198`, called from `emitGamificationEvent` at `:104` on every awarded action) counts rows in `xp_audit_log`:

```ts
"SELECT COALESCE(COUNT(*), 0) AS count FROM xp_audit_log WHERE api_key_id = ? AND action = ?"
```

and compares the result with the thresholds `first-token` 1, `token-consumer` 1,000, `token-machine` 10,000, `token-whale` 100,000 (`events.ts:185-198`). `getActionCount()` in `src/lib/gamification/badges.ts:324-342` does the same for the `action_count` criteria that `evaluateBadges()` reads.

Since #6801 (PR #7260), `cleanupXpAuditLog()` (`src/lib/db/cleanup.ts:348-368`) deletes every `xp_audit_log` row older than `retention.xpAuditLog` days and runs inside `runAutoCleanup()` (`cleanup.ts:460`). The default is 30 days (`src/types/databaseSettings.ts:125`, schema cap 365 in `src/shared/validation/settingsSchemas.ts:573`) and auto-cleanup is on by default.

So with the defaults the badge descriptions in `badges.ts:32-59` ("Made 1,000 API requests", "Made 10,000 API requests", "Made 100,000 API requests") are effectively "made N requests inside the last 30 days". A key that sends 900 requests a month for a year never unlocks Token Consumer; Token Whale needs about 3,300 requests a day, every day. The `token_share` ladder (`generous` 1,000 up to `community-hero` 1,000,000) has the same shape, and the `unique_count` (`badges.ts:349-362`) and `first` (`badges.ts:485-501`, `MIN(created_at)`) criteria read the same pruned table.

**Reproduction** (focused test against `release/v3.8.51`, temp `DATA_DIR`, default retention):

1. Insert 1,200 `xp_audit_log` rows for one key, `action = 'request'`, `created_at = '2026-07-01 12:00:00'`.
2. The `events.ts:178` query returns 1200.
3. `await cleanupXpAuditLog()` returns `{ deleted: 1200 }`; the same query now returns 0.
4. `await emitGamificationEvent({ apiKeyId, action: "request" })` — the query returns 1, `hasBadge(key, "token-consumer")` is `false` although the key has made 1,201 requests.

```
{ before: 1200, deleted: 1200, after: 0 }
{ afterRequest: 1, tokenConsumer: false, firstToken: true }
```

The same sequence with rows dated inside the window unlocks the badge, which is what makes this a retention interaction and not a badge bug.

### Proposed Solution

Two ways to make the counts durable; the choice is yours:

**Option A — durable per-key, per-action counter (recommended).** Add a small `xp_action_counts (api_key_id, action, count, updated_at)` table incremented in `addXp()` (`src/lib/db/gamification.ts:157-174`, the single insert point) in the same statement batch as the audit row, backfilled once from whatever `xp_audit_log` still holds in the migration, and read by both `checkActionCountBadges()` and `getActionCount()`. Retention keeps pruning the audit log; badges no longer depend on it. This mirrors how `user_levels.total_xp` already survives the prune.

**Option B — exclude `xp_audit_log` from the default prune.** Set the default to the 365-day cap or make the row opt-in, and add a note to the retention setting that pruning resets the request badges. Cheapest change, but it only stretches the window and gives back the unbounded growth #6801 wanted to stop.

Either way the badge descriptions and the retention setting's help text should agree on what is being counted.

### Alternatives Considered

- Counting from `call_logs` / usage history instead of the audit log: those tables have their own retention (`callLogs`, `usageHistory` in the same settings block) and are not keyed by gamification action, so the same problem moves rather than disappears.
- Using `user_levels.total_xp / XP per request` as a proxy: XP per action is not constant (anti-cheat can reject awards, `token_share` and `daily_login` add XP) so the derived count drifts.
- Pinning the count on the first row's `id` (`MAX(id) - MIN(id)`): breaks as soon as several keys interleave.

### Acceptance Criteria

- With default retention, a key whose `request` rows are older than 30 days still unlocks `token-consumer` on its 1,000th lifetime request after cleanup has run.
- `cleanupXpAuditLog()` keeps deleting audit rows; `runAutoCleanup()` result shape is unchanged.
- `getActionCount()` and `checkActionCountBadges()` agree on the same source.
- Existing `tests/unit/db-cleanup-xp-audit-log.test.ts` and `tests/unit/gamification/*` stay green.

### Area

Analytics / Usage Tracking, Other (gamification)

### Related Provider(s)

None

### Additional Context

Retention prune introduced by #6801 / #7260. Badge dedup guard: #3472. Sibling gamification issue on the same award path: #12426. Base `release/v3.8.51`, commit `1a0375f`.

### Expected Test Plan

- New unit test that seeds rows outside the window, runs `cleanupXpAuditLog()`, emits one `request` event and asserts the badge unlocks (red on the current base, green with either option).
- Migration test for the backfill if Option A is chosen.
- `tests/unit/db-cleanup-xp-audit-log.test.ts`, `tests/unit/gamification/*.test.ts`, `typecheck:core`, `check:db-rules`.

I can send a PR demonstrating whichever option you prefer.

title: fix(devin): accept Windows sandbox paths in the agentic home check
body:
## Summary

- `isIsolatedHome` (`open-sse/executors/devin-cli-agentic.ts:118-120`) recognized only `/home/bridge` and paths containing `/.sandbox/`. On Windows, `DEVIN_AGENTIC_HOME=C:\Users\...\.sandbox\home` is `path.isAbsolute()`-true but never matches the forward-slash `.sandbox` check, so `buildDevinChildEnv` threw `unsafe_devin_home` (`[500]: DEVIN_AGENTIC_HOME must be an absolute path inside the bridge sandbox`) on every Windows host, whatever the value.
- The helper now normalizes `\` to `/` before comparing (the same approach as `normalizeCommandToken` in `src/lib/acp/registry.ts:283-285`) and is exported as `isIsolatedDevinHome`. Accepted forms: `/home/bridge`, and any absolute path with a `.sandbox` directory segment, on Linux (`/opt/omniroute/.sandbox/home`) and Windows (`C:\Users\x\.sandbox\home`, `D:/omniroute/.sandbox/home`, UNC `\\server\share\.sandbox\home`).
- Deliberately unchanged: `path.isAbsolute()` in `buildDevinChildEnv` still gates absoluteness (a relative `.sandbox` path is still rejected), and `.sandbox` is still required as a directory segment. The issue's example `C:\Users\...\devin-sandbox` does not contain `.sandbox` and is still rejected; the documented Windows form is `<drive>:\...\.sandbox\...`. Accepting an arbitrary configured Windows directory would loosen the fail-closed contract, so it is left as the maintainer's call. `docs/reference/ENVIRONMENT.md:423` notes the Windows form.

## Related Issues

- Closes #12405
- Related to #11240

## Validation

Accepts `C:\Users\example\.sandbox\home`, a nested `.sandbox\devin-sandbox\home`, `D:/omniroute/.sandbox/home`, UNC `\\server\share\.sandbox\home`, `/home/bridge`, `/opt/omniroute/.sandbox/unit-home`; rejects `C:\Users\example`, `C:\Users\example\devin-sandbox`, `C:\Users\example\.sandbox` (no trailing segment), `C:\Users\example\sandbox\home`, `/tmp/outside`, `/home/bridge2`, `""`; and asserts through `buildDevinChildEnv` that `relative/.sandbox/home` still throws. title: fix(orchestration): keep the first staleSince while a source keeps failing
body:
## Summary

- `buildSourceStatuses` (`src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/orchestration/hooks/useOrchestrationSnapshot.ts:63-90`) stamps every failed source with the current poll's `nowIso` (lines 76, 79, 87), and the poll loop replaced the whole list with `setStatuses(next)`. With the `sourceStale` message now live, `SourceNode` (`nodes/SourceNode.tsx:24-28`) therefore read "stale since <last poll>" instead of the first error, and because `snapshotContentKey` serialises `s.sources`, the key changed on every 5s/30s tick for as long as a source was down — re-minting the node/edge arrays the `React.memo` gate exists to protect.
- This is the second bullet of #12392 ("`staleSince` avança a cada poll"). Fix: a pure `carryStaleSince(prev, next)` helper (line 99) copies the previous `staleSince` onto a source that was already failing, applied through the functional update `setStatuses((prev) => carryStaleSince(prev, next))` (line 152). A source that recovers is pushed as `{ ok: true }` with no `staleSince`, so the next failure is stamped fresh; a first failure keeps this poll's `nowIso`. `buildSourceStatuses`, `mergeSnapshot` and the conductor `offline` branch are untouched.
- Deliberately out of scope: the other bullets of #12392 (toolbar debounce race, placeholder-only stale indicator in `mergeSnapshot`, a11y, `noMatches`, particle budget, drawer error banner, `toggleCsv`) — each is a separate surface and the issue stays open.

## Related Issues

- Refs #12392 (second checklist item; the issue has further bullets and stays open)

## Validation

Asserts no `staleSince` on the healthy poll, a string on the first failure, the SAME value on the next failing poll 5s later (base fails here: `expected '…:18.927Z' to be '…:13.927Z'`), snapshot referential identity preserved across the two failing polls, and `staleSince` cleared on recovery. title: fix(video): clamp estimateJpegFrameBytes, reuse the shared JPEG prefix
body:
## Summary

- `estimateJpegFrameBytes` (`src/lib/guardrails/videoBridgeFrameContract.ts:24-27`) subtracted the padding count from the floored estimate with no floor of its own, so the padding-only payloads the charset-only pattern admits (`data:image/jpeg;base64,=` and `==`) came back as `-1`. Consequence-free in today's upper-bound usage, as #12323 notes, but a documented byte estimate never goes negative: the return is now `Math.max(0, ...)` (item 1).
- The three encode sites named in the issue (`videoBridgeContactSheet.ts:123`, `videoBridgeRuntime.ts:1000`, `videoBridgeDrilldownLifecycle.ts:173`) still built their frame data URIs from a hardcoded `data:image/jpeg;base64,` template literal; they now import `JPEG_FRAME_DATA_URI_PREFIX` from the shared contract (item 2). Byte-for-byte identical output, since the constant is the same literal.
- Deliberately out of scope: item 3 (`videoBridgeBrokerClient.ts:104`, the case-sensitive broker-output regex) and item 4 (structural base64 validation). Both are behaviour decisions per the issue text, so the issue stays open; this PR is `Refs`, not `Closes`. `videoBridgeRuntime.ts` gains a single import of the zero-dependency contract module, so no import cycle is introduced (`videoBridgeContactSheet.ts` already imported both).

title: fix(compression): terminate idle workers instead of dropping them
body:
## Summary

- `CompressionWorkerPool.finish()` (`open-sse/services/compression/compressionWorkerPool.ts:188`) evicted an idle worker with `this.remove(slot, false)`, and `remove()` (`:198-203`) only called `worker.terminate()` `if (terminate)`. The idle path therefore deleted the slot from the pool set but never terminated the thread; `compressionWorker.ts:13` keeps a `parentPort.on("message")` listener, so the worker's event loop and V8 isolate stayed alive forever, and `dispatch()` (`:156`) spawned a replacement because `workers.size < size`. The `OMNI_COMPRESSION_WORKERS` cap held in bookkeeping only: every idle cycle leaked one live thread. This is the mechanism confirmed on #11804 (request-driven thread growth, ~90 threads parked in `ep_poll`, RSS far outside the main heap) and the one-line patch the reporter measured on a live instance: 57 leaked workers / 72 threads / 5.77 GB climbing before, 0 leaked / 15 threads / 846 MB flat after.
- `remove()` now always terminates the thread. The `terminate` parameter is removed rather than flipped at the idle call site: `close()` and `fail()` already passed `true`, so the parameter only existed to express the buggy case. A short comment on `remove()` records why dropping the slot alone is not enough. `close()`, `fail()`, timeouts and the queue/dispatch logic are otherwise unchanged; `terminate()` failures are still swallowed as before.
- Out of scope, on purpose: the `callLogArtifactWorker` hypothesis raised mid-thread (later marked unconfirmed by its author), the six bundled copies of the pool in the Next.js server chunks (they pick this change up at build time), and any change to the idle timeout or pool size defaults.

## Related Issues

- Closes #11804
- Related to #12245 (the combo loop-safety timer leak reported on the same issue, already merged)

## Validation

- [x] Change type: other (compression worker pool, `open-sse/`)
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path: `tests/unit/compression/compression-worker.test.ts` + `tests/unit/compression/compression-worker-file-resolution.test.ts` 17/17 (4 suites), `node scripts/check/check-complexity-ratchets.mjs --base-ref origin/release/v3.8.51` OK (0 violations, base 0), `npm run check:changelog-integrity` OK, `npm run typecheck:core` exit 0
- [ ] `npm run lint` — eslint run on the two touched source files only (`--suppressions-location config/quality/eslint-suppressions.json`), exit 0; the repository-wide command was not run
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base `release/v3.8.51` (`1a0375fba`); focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR
- SonarQube is temporarily opt-in while the private project has no quota; it is not a PR gate.

Red/green: the new case fails on the base with `idle eviction must terminate the worker thread: 0 !== 1` and passes with the change (three consecutive runs, 8/8 in the file).

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/compression/compression-worker.test.ts` (1 new case, "terminates an idle worker instead of only dropping it from the pool"): spies on `Worker.prototype.terminate` and `Worker.prototype.postMessage` around a local `{ size: 1, idleMs: 50 }` pool, runs one job, waits past the idle window, and asserts that exactly one worker was spawned, that `terminate()` was called once, and that the process does not retain the worker's `MessagePort` (`process.getActiveResourcesInfo()`). The `finally` block restores both prototypes, closes the pool, and terminates any worker the pool forgot, so a future regression fails the assertion instead of keeping the test runner alive. The seven existing cases are untouched.
- No `stryker.conf.json` change: `open-sse/services/compression/` is not in the `mutate` list.

## Coverage Notes

- `open-sse/services/compression/compressionWorkerPool.ts`: the idle path of `finish()` and the unconditional `terminate()` in `remove()` are exercised by the new case; `close()` by the new case's `finally` and the existing timeout case; `fail()` by the existing "fails open" case. No touched file lost coverage.

## Reviewer Notes

- Behavioural change is limited to idle eviction: the thread is now terminated at the moment it is removed from the set, which is what `close()` and `fail()` already did. Nothing about job routing changes, so a request arriving after eviction still gets a freshly spawned worker exactly as before.
- Anyone patching an installed 3.8.50/3.8.51 bundle by hand should note that the minified idle call site appears in five files (four Next.js runtime chunks plus `open-sse/mcp-server/server.js`), as documented on the issue; a normal build from this branch covers all of them.
- No migrations, feature flags, or env changes.

title: fix(gemini): strip prefixItems from Gemini tool schemas
body:
## Summary

- `GEMINI_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_KEYS` (`open-sse/translator/helpers/geminiHelper.ts:9-105` on the base) is the only strip-list `cleanJSONSchemaForAntigravity` applies to tool parameter schemas (`removeUnsupportedKeywords`, `geminiHelper.ts:643`), and it did not contain the JSON-Schema-2020-12 tuple keyword `prefixItems`. Claude Code's built-in tools describe `[start_line, end_line]` ranges as a tuple nested under `items`, so every tool-bearing Claude Code request routed to a Gemini model was rejected before generation with `400 Invalid JSON payload received. Unknown name "prefixItems" at 'tools[0].function_declarations[1].parameters.properties[5].value.properties[0].value.items': Cannot find field` (#12509). All three tool shapes that `buildGeminiTools` accepts go through the same cleaner (`geminiToolsSanitizer.ts:207`, `:220` for Claude `input_schema`, `:238` for OpenAI `function.parameters`), so the Claude Messages compatibility path the reporter uses and the OpenAI path were both affected.
- Before: `prefixItems` survived at every nesting level (top-level array property, sibling of `items`, and the reporter's tuple under `items`) and reached Gemini verbatim. After: `prefixItems` is added to `GEMINI_UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_KEYS` next to `uniqueItems` (#9617), so it is removed recursively at every level, the same way `multipleOf`, `strict` and `encrypted` already are. When the tuple carried `items: false` (the 2020-12 idiom for "no extra elements"), Phase 8 `ensureArrayItems` (`geminiHelper.ts:733` on the base) already injects `{ type: "string" }`, so the parameter stays a valid Gemini array with an `items` schema; when a regular `items` schema sits next to `prefixItems`, that `items` schema is kept untouched.
- Deliberately out of scope: promoting `prefixItems[0]` into `items` (the tuple's element types can differ, and Gemini has no way to express positional typing, so the safe default `items` schema is the honest translation); touching `UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA_CONSTRAINTS` beyond what it already derives from the Set; any change to the Antigravity envelope or to response schemas.

## Related Issues

- Closes #12509
- Related to #9617 (same class of fix, `uniqueItems`)
- Related to #12310 (touches the same file; see Reviewer Notes)

## Validation

Choose the change type and focused loop from the
[Contribution Golden Path](../docs/ops/CONTRIBUTION_GOLDEN_PATH.md). The full unit suite,
Vitest, the 60% coverage gate, and the production build all run in CI on this PR (#8329):

title: Test suite scale is unefficient: ~4.4k test files waste build and test time
body:
## Problem

The test suite has grown to an inefficient scale that wastes build and test time locally and in CI:

- `tests/unit": 4,299 files; `tests/integration": 127 files; TypeScript under `tests/": ~5,036 files (CodeGraph index).
- 30+ `test:*` npm scripts across 4 runners (`node:test`, 2x Vitest configs, Playwright) plus shard/serial/live variants.
- Discovery globs in `test:unit`/`test:coverage:runner` enumerate the same large file sets repeatedly, so sharding, coverage, and local iteration all pay the full cost.

## Impact

- Long local iteration (`test:unit`, `test:coverage`) and CI shard fan-out for what should be fast unit feedback.
- High maintenance cost: naming/folder conventions drifted (`tests/unit/*` flat + 25+ subfolders + `dashboard/` + `serial/`), live/e2e/boundary tests mixed near unit tests.
- Coverage gate (60/60/60/60) runs over the whole set, amplifying the cost of every run.

## Proposal (audit + cleanup plan)

1. Audit: duplicate/overlapping suites (chatcore/combo/translator), dead or live-only tests hiding in unit paths, slowest files.
2. Consolidate: merge near-duplicate suites, move live/e2e/boundary out of unit globs, unify naming/folder rules.
3. Split execution tiers: fast unit (default) vs integration vs live/e2e, so `npm run test:unit` stays fast.
4. No coverage regression: keep 60/60/60/60 gate green; update baselines only on genuine improvement.

 Happy to take this on starting from `release/v3.8.51`.

title: fix(audio): resolve combo names on /v1/audio/translations
body:
## Summary

- `POST /v1/audio/translations` rejected combo names that `GET /v1/models` advertises. On the base, `src/app/api/v1/audio/translations/route.ts:68-77` hands the raw `model` string to `parseTranslationModel()` and returns `400 Invalid translation model: <combo>. Use format: provider/model` when it is not a `provider/model` id; nothing calls `getComboByName()` first. Every sibling already resolves combos: chat, embeddings, `/v1/audio/transcriptions` (#9134, fixed by #9382 at `src/app/api/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts:183-212`), `/v1/audio/speech` and `/v1/videos/generations` (#10469, fixed by #10471). Translations was the one route those fixes did not cover, so the same combo name with the same file worked on `/v1/audio/transcriptions` and failed on `/v1/audio/translations`.
- Before: `model=traducao` (a `priority` combo over `localstt/whisper-1`) → `400 Invalid translation model: traducao. Use format: provider/model`, no upstream call. After: one upstream call to `http://localhost:9000/v1/audio/translations` whose multipart `model` is `whisper-1`; the response is the upstream body. Literal `provider/model` ids skip the lookup and unknown bare names keep the existing 400 and format hint.
- The change mirrors the transcriptions route exactly. The single-target body of `POST` moves unchanged into `translateWithModel(formData, modelStr, startTime)`; after `enforceApiKeyPolicy`, a bare name (no `/`) is looked up with `getComboByName()` and, when it is a combo, fanned out through `handleComboChat()` with one multipart copy per target (`withModel()` copies every field and replaces only `model`; the uploaded Blob is reused). Unknown bare names and literal ids fall through to `translateWithModel()` as before. No handler, registry, provider, schema or response-shape change.
- Deliberately out of scope: the alias-candidate credential fallback that transcriptions has (`audioModelAliasCandidates` / `findAlternateAudioProvider`) is not added here, since translations never had it and it is a separate behavior; `withModel()` and the combo block are duplicated from the transcriptions route rather than lifted into `_shared/`, to keep this diff mirror-shaped and reviewable against #9382 (a follow-up could factor both routes onto one helper).

## Related Issues

- Closes: no open issue for this route (open issues and PRs searched for `audio translations combo`; none found).
- Related to #9134 and #9382 (transcriptions), #10469 and #10471 (speech and videos), #5809 (the translations endpoint).

## Validation

Choose the change type and focused loop from the
[Contribution Golden Path](../docs/ops/CONTRIBUTION_GOLDEN_PATH.md). The full unit suite,
Vitest, the 60% coverage gate, and the production build all run in CI on this PR (#8329):

- [x] Change type: routing
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path: `tests/unit/audio-translations-combo-resolution.test.ts` 3/3; neighbours `audio-transcriptions-combo-resolution`, `9134-repro-audio-combo-rejection`, `video-combo-route`, `audio-translations-route`, `audio-transcription-handler`, `audio-provider-nodes-selection`, `audio-speech-dynamic-node-9096`, `audio-alias-prefix-10586`, `audio-nested-model-credential-fallback` and `tests/unit/combo/*` 252/252; `node scripts/check/check-complexity-ratchets.mjs --base-ref origin/release/v3.8.51` OK (0 new violations); `npm run check:changelog-integrity` OK; `npm run typecheck:core` exit 0; `eslint` and `prettier --check` on the two touched TypeScript files exit 0
- [ ] `npm run lint`
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base `release/v3.8.51`; focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR
- SonarQube is temporarily opt-in while the private project has no quota; it is not a PR gate.

Red/green: with the base `route.ts` swapped in, the combo case fails with `400 Invalid translation model: traducao. Use format: provider/model` (actual 400, expected 200) and the other two cases pass; with the change all three pass.

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/audio-translations-combo-resolution.test.ts` (new, 3 cases): creates a real `openai-compatible` provider node (`prefix: localstt`, `apiType: audio-transcriptions`) and a `priority` combo `traducao` in the test database, stubs `globalThis.fetch`, and asserts at the upstream sink. (2) `model=localstt/whisper-1` → dispatched directly, same URL, multipart `model=whisper-1`. (3) `model=definitely-not-a-combo-or-model` → 400 with `Invalid translation model`, zero upstream calls.
