title: fix(claude): Fable 5.1 rejected on the native OAuth path — pinned claude-cli version is below Anthropic's 2.1.251 gate

labels.name: backlog
labels.description: Tracked for future work; not blocking

body:
## Summary

Claude Fable 5.1 (`claude-fable-5-1`, GA 2026-09-01) cannot be served through the native `claude` OAuth provider. Anthropic rejects the request on the Claude Code client version OmniRoute advertises, and that version is a bare constant with no environment override.

## Reproduce

`POST /api/v1/messages` through the gateway, on a Claude Max OAuth connection:

```json
{"model":"claude/claude-fable-5-1","max_tokens":16,
 "messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly: PONG"}]}
```

Response:

```json
{"error":{"message":"[400]: Claude Code 2.1.219 does not support this model; version 2.1.251 or newer is required. Run 'claude update', or update the Claude desktop app, then try again.","type":"invalid_request_error","code":"bad_request"}}
```

Control, same API key, same connection, seconds later — a combo targeting `claude/claude-fable-5` returns `200` with `"model":"claude-fable-5"` and the expected completion.

So the model id reaches Anthropic intact and the OAuth rail is healthy. What is refused is the advertised client version.

## Root cause

`src/shared/constants/claudeCodeClient.ts` on `main`:

```ts
export const CLAUDE_CODE_CLIENT_VERSION = "2.1.220";
export const CLAUDE_CODE_CLIENT_BUILD_REVISION = "1f2";
```

The published 3.8.49 build carries `2.1.219` / `250`. Anthropic's gate for this model is `>= 2.1.251`, so both the released build and the current `main` are below it.

There is no escape hatch on the Claude path. `CLAUDE_USER_AGENT` overrides only the User-Agent string in `buildHeaders()`, while the constant additionally feeds `open-sse/config/anthropicHeaders.ts`, `open-sse/executors/claudeIdentity.ts`, `open-sse/config/claudeCodeCompatibleIdentity.ts` and `open-sse/services/ccBridgeTransforms.ts`. Codex has `CODEX_CLIENT_VERSION` for exactly this situation; Claude has no equivalent.

Consequence: every Claude Max / Claude Pro user is locked out of Fable 5.1 through OmniRoute until a release re-captures the CLI, with no configuration workaround.

## Suggested fix

1. Capture a `claude-cli` release `>= 2.1.251` and bump the constants in lockstep — `tests/unit/claude-codex-identity-version-sync.test.ts` already guards the 4 sources.
2. Optionally add a `CLAUDE_CODE_CLIENT_VERSION` environment override mirroring `CODEX_CLIENT_VERSION`, so the next model gated on a client version can be unblocked without waiting for a release. This is the part that turns a recurring outage into a config change.

## Environment

- OmniRoute 3.8.49, installed globally via npm
- macOS 15 (Darwin 25.6.0), arm64
- Native `claude` provider, Claude Max OAuth connection, combo strategy `headroom`
- No `CLI_COMPAT_*` flags set

title: fix(auth): antigravity oauth advertises redirect_uri=http://localhost:8080/callback but never binds the port

labels.name: backlog
labels.description: Tracked for future work; not blocking

body:
## Summary

`omniroute oauth start --provider antigravity` builds its Google authorize URL with

```
redirect_uri=http%3A%2F%2Flocalhost%3A8080%2Fcallback
```

but nothing ever listens on port 8080. After the user consents, Google redirects the browser to `http://localhost:8080/callback?state=…&code=…` and they land on **ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED**.

The flow does in fact work — it wants the callback URL pasted back at its `Callback URL or code:` prompt — but nothing on the error page says so. It reads as a failed authorization.

## Environment

- OmniRoute v3.8.50 (npm global install)
- Windows 11
- Provider: `antigravity` (flow type `browser` per `omniroute oauth providers`)

## Repro

1. `omniroute oauth start --provider antigravity`
2. Complete Google consent in the browser.
3. Browser redirects to `localhost:8080/callback?...` → **ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED**.

Port 8080 was verified free **before** launching the flow and remained unbound **while the CLI sat at its prompt**:

```
netstat -ano | findstr ":8080 " | findstr LISTENING   ->  0 results
```

So this is not a port conflict — no listener is ever started.

## Expected

Either:

- **(a)** bind a short-lived local server on the advertised port to capture `code` automatically and close the loop, or
- **(b)** don't advertise a `localhost` redirect at all — use an out-of-band redirect that renders the code for copying.

**(b) is already implemented correctly for `claude-code`**, which uses

```
redirect_uri=https://platform.claude.com/oauth/code/callback
```

and lands the user on a page that *displays* the code to paste. That flow is not confusing. The antigravity flow promises a loopback capture it never performs.

## Actual

Every user of the antigravity browser flow hits a browser error page mid-authorization and has to know, without being told, to copy the URL out of the address bar and paste it back into the terminal.

## Workaround

Copy the full `localhost:8080/callback?...` URL from the address bar and paste it at the `Callback URL or code:` prompt. The connection then completes normally — confirmed working with a live call afterwards:

```
omniroute chat --model "antigravity/gemini-3.1-flash-lite" "Reply with the single word: ok"
ok
[gemini-3.1-flash-lite · 1670ms · 243 tok]
```

## Minor, possibly related

The model ids reported by `omniroute models antigravity` are display names (`Claude Sonnet 4.6 (Thinking)`, `Gemini 3.7 Flash (High)`), and passing them verbatim to `chat` fails — silently, with no output and no error. Only slug forms such as `antigravity/gemini-3.1-flash-lite` work. Same for `ds`: the table prints `DeepSeek V4 Flash` while the API wants `deepseek-v4-flash`. Whatever the intended contract, the column heading "Model ID" is misleading if the value cannot be used as one.

title: fix(claude): config set claude replaces ~/.claude/settings.json wholesale — destroys unrelated Claude Code settings
body:
## Summary

`omniroute config set claude` does not merge into `~/.claude/settings.json` — it **replaces the entire file** with OmniRoute's own 3-key format, destroying every unrelated Claude Code setting.

This is silent data loss on a config file OmniRoute does not own.

## Environment

- OmniRoute v3.8.49 (npm global install)
- Windows 11, Node.js 24+
- Claude Code v2.1.221

## Repro

`~/.claude/settings.json` before — 11 top-level keys:

```
agentPushNotifEnabled, autoUpdatesChannel, effortLevel, enableWorkflows,
enabledPlugins, env, extraKnownMarketplaces, hooks, model,
skipWorkflowUsageWarning, statusLine
```

Run:

```
omniroute config set claude --model claude-fallback --yes --non-interactive
```

Output:

```
Backup saved to: C:\Users\<user>\.claude\.omniroute.bak\settings.json.bak
✔ Config written to C:\Users\<user>\.claude\settings.json
```

After — 3 keys, 159 bytes total:

```json
{ "authToken": "...", "baseUrl": "...", "models": ... }
```

## Expected

Only the keys OmniRoute manages (`env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `env.ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, `env.ANTHROPIC_SMALL_FAST_MODEL`, and/or `model`) should be written, leaving everything else byte-identical.

## Actual

`hooks`, `enabledPlugins`, `statusLine`, `model`, `effortLevel`, `extraKnownMarketplaces`, `enableWorkflows`, `agentPushNotifEnabled`, `autoUpdatesChannel`, `skipWorkflowUsageWarning` are all gone.

Notably the written file is not even a valid Claude Code settings shape — `authToken` / `baseUrl` / `models` are not keys Claude Code reads, so the resulting config is inert for its stated purpose *and* destructive.

## Impact

Anyone running this against a real Claude Code install loses their hooks, plugins and status line with no prompt indicating the file will be replaced rather than updated. `--non-interactive`/`--yes` make it easy to hit from a script.

Mitigating factor: the `.omniroute.bak/settings.json.bak` copy quoted in the output does let you recover, if you notice.

## Note on version

Observed on 3.8.49. I have not retested on 3.8.50 because reproducing it destroys the file, and this is a live machine — happy to retest if that would help.

title: fix(chatCore): stop executeWithUpstreamStartTimeout leaking its abortPromise listener (hedge-cancelled process exit)
body:
## Summary

Fixes the `Error [AbortError]: hedge-cancelled` process exit (exit code 7) seen on a production instance on 2026-08-31, and hardens the process crash guard around it.

**Root cause** (mapped from the built chunks back to source and reproduced): `executeWithUpstreamStartTimeout` in `open-sse/handlers/chatCore/upstreamTimeouts.ts` registered a `{ once: true }` abort listener for `abortPromise` on the long-lived client/stream signal and never removed it in `finally`, so every executor attempt (and every retry) leaked one listener. `Promise.race` only subscribes once the array literal has been evaluated; when `execute()` threw synchronously the race never ran, `abortPromise` was orphaned, and the next hedge cancellation / client disconnect aborted the signal with the string reason that `streamHandler.ts` forwards. `createAbortError()` rebuilt it as an `AbortError`-named Error and rejected a promise nothing awaited. That `unhandledRejection` reached `src/shared/utils/httpClientAbortGuard.mjs`, whose handler re-threw it as an `uncaughtException`, and the process exited.

## Commits

1. `fix(sse): stop mergeAbortSignals from leaking abort listeners` - the listener-hygiene change from #12391 (`open-sse/executors/base.ts`), included so this branch is self-contained. Note: that change is correct but is **not** on the crash path above.
2. `fix(server): stop the crash guard re-throwing combo abort reasons` - `isClientAbortError()` now absorbs `AbortError`s and the combo abort reasons from `comboAbortReasons.ts` (`hedge-cancelled`, `combo-per-model-timeout`). Ports the upstream guard tests and makes the child-process tests Windows-portable (a `file://` URL instead of a bare path in dynamic `import()`).
3. `fix(chatCore): stop executeWithUpstreamStartTimeout leaking its abortPromise listener` - the root-cause fix: keep a handle to the listener and remove it with the others in `finally`; mark the two race-loser promises as handled so a synchronous throw from `execute()` can never orphan them. Race semantics are unchanged.
4. `fix(server): absorb raw string abort reasons in the crash guard; document the verified crash path` - `streamHandler.ts` aborts with raw string reasons and undici rejects with `signal.reason` verbatim, so a cancellation can reach process level as a bare string; the guard now absorbs those too. Comments corrected to describe the verified mechanism.

## Tests

- New regression tests in `tests/unit/chatcore-upstream-timeouts.test.ts` (+2; both fail against the previous implementation: one asserts no listener growth after a resolving `execute`, one asserts that a synchronously throwing `execute` followed by a late `hedge-cancelled` abort produces no `unhandledRejection`).
- `tests/unit/httpClientAbortGuard.test.mjs` (+9), including a real child-process replay of the production shape on both the `uncaughtException` and `unhandledRejection` routes, and a genuine-error case that must still crash.
- Results: `httpClientAbortGuard` 18/18, `chatcore-upstream-timeouts` 7/7, `executor-base-utils` 23/23; 127 related unit test files 968/970 (the 2 failures reproduce identically on the base commit: a stale G13 golden and a Windows temp-dir EPERM on cleanup).
- `tsc --noEmit -p open-sse/tsconfig.json` clean; eslint clean on the changed files.

## Related

- Extends #12391, which on its own does not fix the exit.
- Separately observed on Windows and not addressed here: `scripts/build/bootstrap-env.mjs` resolves `DATA_DIR` to `%APPDATA%\omniroute` while `src/lib/dataPaths.ts` prefers a legacy `~/.omniroute` when it exists, so the first `npm start` of a source checkout can auto-generate a new `STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and orphan every previously encrypted credential. Happy to file it as an issue.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(providers): Devin Claude Bridge fails on Windows — DEVIN_AGENTIC_HOME sandbox check rejects all Windows paths
body:
## Summary

The Devin Claude Bridge executor rejects `DEVIN_AGENTIC_HOME` on Windows, so Devin bridge models
(e.g. `dva/swe-1-7-lightning`) fail on Windows with:

```
[500]: DEVIN_AGENTIC_HOME must be an absolute path inside the bridge sandbox
```

## Root cause

`open-sse/executors/devin-cli-agentic.ts:118-119`:

```ts
function isIsolatedHome(value: string): boolean {
  return value === "/home/bridge" || value.includes("/.sandbox/");
}
```

`buildDevinChildEnv` (same file, line 127) throws unless `DEVIN_AGENTIC_HOME` is absolute AND
passes `isIsolatedHome()`. The check only recognizes Linux-style sandbox paths
(`/home/bridge`, anything containing `/.sandbox/`). A Windows path such as `C:\Users\...\devin-sandbox`
is `path.isAbsolute()`-true but never matches `isIsolatedHome()`, so the bridge always fails
closed on Windows regardless of what `DEVIN_AGENTIC_HOME` is set to.

## Expected behavior

`isIsolatedHome()` (or its caller) should recognize a valid isolated home on Windows too — e.g.
accept a configured Windows sandbox directory the same way `/home/bridge`/`/.sandbox/` are
accepted on Linux — instead of unconditionally rejecting every Windows absolute path.

## Reported via

OmniRoute Discord support channel (support-mesh @-mention triage).

body:

## Summary

The Devin Claude bridge installs a *real* Claude Code CLI inside its image. It was still pinned at `2.1.220` while the Claude identity OmniRoute impersonates moved to `2.1.258` in #12344 (for Fable 5.1). This raises the bridge pin to the same generation — the first CLI line that knows the Fable 5.1 tier natively — so the containerized CLI matches the fingerprint the executor emits.

**Scope note.** The pin only affects the containerized CLI. OmniRoute strips the client's `x-anthropic-billing-header` line and rewrites the `User-Agent` on the Claude OAuth path (`open-sse/executors/base.ts`), so Anthropic's `2.1.251 or newer` gate never sees the bridge's own CLI version. This is alignment, not a fix for that 400.

## What changed

- `docker/devin-bridge/Dockerfile` — `ARG CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION` default `2.1.220` → `2.1.258`.
- `docker/devin-bridge/compose.yml` — the shared `x-runtime` build arg, same bump (covers `omniroute`, `claude`, `contract` and the live services).
- `docs/DEVIN_CLAUDE_BRIDGE.md` — architecture line + status callout. The callout now states that the offline/live validation on record was performed on `2.1.220`, and lists what was and was not re-run on the new pin.
- `CHANGELOG.md` — `[Unreleased]` → 📝 Maintenance entry.

## Validation

On the pinned base image (`node:26.0.0-bookworm-slim`, arm64):

- `docker compose -f docker/devin-bridge/compose.yml --profile offline config` — valid; `CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION: 2.1.258` resolved in all three services.
- `scripts/devin-bridge/verify-anthropic-isolation --static` — PASS.
- `npm run check:docs-all` green; prettier clean.

**Not re-run (needs a larger Docker VM):** the offline mock e2e (`scripts/devin-bridge/test-e2e-mock`) and the three-scenario live suite. `scripts/devin-bridge/build` failed at the `npm run build` layer with `ResourceExhausted` on an 8 GB Docker Desktop VM — a layer this PR does not touch. Steps 3–5 of "Updating pinned tools" in the doc remain open, and the doc callout says so explicitly.

## Devin CLI

Unchanged (`3000.2.17`, archive checksums untouched).

title: feat(deploy): Kubernetes support for k3s and k8s
body:
## Summary

The repo ships `docker-compose.yml` and `fly.toml`, and `DOCKER_GUIDE.md` already warns that "stock Docker / Kubernetes OmniRoute is one Node process + one SQLite writer" — but there are no manifests. Anyone running this on k3s or k8s writes them from scratch, against a topology whose constraints are invisible until they bite:

- a second replica against the same volume corrupts the database;
- an ingress that buffers responses withholds the SSE stream until the provider turn ends, which reads as a hung request, not as broken streaming;
- a liveness probe pointed at `/api/monitoring/health` does real DB work on every kubelet tick and restarts the only pod under load.

So the topology is **encoded, not documented**. `replicas: 1`, `Recreate` and `ReadWriteOnce` are fixed in the base, in the chart and in the generator — not exposed as options anywhere. And the chart and the spec schema refuse to render a configuration that fails at runtime, naming the field rather than emitting something that breaks later:

| Rejected | Because |
| --- | --- |
| `replicaCount > 1` | two pods on one volume corrupt the SQLite file |
| access mode ≠ `ReadWriteOnce` | a shared-write volume invites the same second writer |
| heap ceiling ≥ memory limit | the kernel OOM-kills the pod instead of Node raising a recoverable heap error (#7849) |
| `shutdownTimeoutMs` ≥ grace − preStop | the kubelet SIGKILLs mid-drain, so in-flight SSE is cut rather than drained |
| TLS with no Ingress | terminating TLS at something that does not exist |

Four artifacts, one topology:

- **`deploy/kubernetes/`** — Kustomize base plus k3s (Traefik + `local-path`) and generic k8s (ingress-nginx) overlays.
- **`deploy/helm/omniroute/`** — the same topology, values-driven.
- **`omniroute deploy k8s`** — prints manifests built from a running instance's settings, so ports, origins and flags are not transcribed by hand. It writes to stdout and touches nothing, so it composes: `omniroute deploy k8s --target local | kubectl apply -f -`.
- **`docs/ops/KUBERNETES_DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md`** — 416 lines covering deploy, ingress/SSE, probes, upgrades, storage/backups, sizing and troubleshooting.

`local` and `vps` differ only in defaults. `local` assumes k3s on the same machine. `vps` assumes a hostname in front of a cluster other people can reach, so TLS is on, `REQUIRE_API_KEY=true`, the cluster's default StorageClass binds, and `LIVE_WS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS` is derived from the host — without that, the dashboard's live view is rejected by the origin check on the very host it is served from.

Probes follow `docs/ops/MONITORING_GUIDE.md` ("Kubernetes probe recommendations", merged in #10297): `/healthz` for startup and readiness, `/livez` for liveness, never `/api/monitoring/health`. The nginx overlay disables response buffering; the Traefik idle-timeout caveat is documented for k3s, since that one is an entrypoint setting and not an Ingress annotation.

**Provisioning is advisory on purpose.** `omniroute deploy k8s provision` prints the k3s commands and never runs them or connects to a server. Doing it directly would mean shipping an SSH client and holding a private key — a standing surface for a one-off task — so it follows the shape `contrib/vps` already uses for a VPS install. The VPS plan covers the two steps easiest to get wrong by hand: `--tls-san`, without which the cluster is only reachable as `127.0.0.1` and a remote `kubectl` fails TLS verification, and rewriting the `127.0.0.1` server address in the kubeconfig k3s writes. Values rendered into those commands are constrained to hostname, version, username and context shapes, so a printed command cannot mean something other than what it looks like.

**No new API route and no new dashboard surface.** An earlier draft put this behind `/api/deploy/*` with a UI tab; it was dropped before landing. Applying manifests by clicking is at odds with GitOps — the desired state should be versioned, not produced by a form — and the routes existed only to serve the button, spawning `kubectl` with the host kubeconfig, which is a full cluster credential. The CLI reaches the same result without that surface, so `routeGuard.ts` is untouched.

**Two fixes to the manifests themselves**, both surfaced by the test that pins the generator against `deploy/kubernetes/base`:

- Dropped `API_PORT` from the base ConfigMap. Setting it moves the API to a separate port (`src/lib/runtime/ports.ts:27`) that neither the container nor the Service exposes, leaving that listener unreachable. Unset, the API and dashboard share `PORT` — which is what the manifests actually expose.
- Made the container port protocol explicit, so the committed manifest and the generator agree byte for byte.

`deploy` also joins `--mcp` in reserving stdout for data (`bin/omniroute.mjs`). Env-loading notices there made the YAML unparseable — `control characters are not allowed` — which broke the pipe the command exists for.

## Related Issues

- Related to #10297 — the probe recommendations these manifests implement
- Related to #7849 — the V8-heap-vs-cgroup ceiling the spec schema now enforces
- Related to #8075 — multi-writer HA; until it ships, single-replica is the documented ceiling and this PR encodes it

## Validation

- [x] Change type: build-deploy (plus CLI)
- [x] Focused tests and category gates from the golden path
- [x] `npm run lint`
- [x] Reconciled with the current active release base; focused checks rerun afterward
- [x] Production-code changes include a new or updated automated test in this PR

**Applied to a live cluster, not just a dry run.** Single-node k3s v1.36.4+k3s1:

| Checked | Result |
| --- | --- |
| PVC on `local-path` | `Bound`, 10Gi, RWO |
| Pod | `1/1 Running`, 0 restarts |
| Rollout | completed, `Available=True` |
| `/healthz` and `/livez` through the Service | HTTP 200 both |
| `/v1/models` | answers application JSON, so the app serves — not just the probes |
| Probe failure events | none recorded |
| Helm chart, `--dry-run=server` | accepted by the real API server |

That run corrected two documentation errors a client-side dry run cannot catch: the health check used `wget`, and the published image ships neither `wget` nor `curl` (`node` is the only HTTP client in it); and an Ingress naming an IngressClass the cluster does not run is accepted by the API server and then silently routes nothing. Both are now in the guide, the second as a troubleshooting row.

Red first, per invariant: each manifest guard was verified to fail under a deliberate mutation of the file it protects — flipping `replicas` to 2, the access mode to RWX, `proxy-buffering` to `on`, liveness to `/api/monitoring/health`, or the shutdown budget past the grace period each turns exactly one test red, and only one. The generator/CLI suites found three real defects while being written: a `fail` placed at the top level of a `_*.tpl` file (Helm parses and discards it, so the replica guard was a silent no-op), context-name validation that rejected legitimate EKS contexts, and the stdout pollution above.

The automated review then found four more, fixed in the second commit: an address pattern that accepted a port or a bare IPv6 literal and rendered `https://host:123:6443`; a context pattern that rejected the ARN-shaped contexts managed clusters produce; the context being interpolated into a temp path, which the previous item would have turned into a directory traversal; and a quantity pattern that accepted `K` while rejecting `k`, the lowercase decimal thousand Kubernetes actually uses, so `512k` was refused. Each has a regression case.

Rebased onto `release/v3.8.51` and the full set rerun there: **54 tests passing**, `npm run typecheck:core` clean, both overlays render with zero kustomize warnings, `helm lint` clean, `check:docs-all` / `check:tracked-artifacts` / `check:cli-i18n` passing, and `omniroute deploy k8s | kubectl apply --dry-run=client -f -` still creates all six objects.

`npm run lint` reports **zero errors** but exits 2, on this branch and on an untouched checkout of the base alike — `suppressions left that do not occur anymore`, unrelated to any file here.

## Tests Added Or Updated

- `tests/unit/k8s-deploy-manifests.test.ts` — 12 cases over the committed manifests: single replica, Recreate, RWO, probe targets, drain budget, unbuffered SSE, secret hygiene, and that the chart's replica guard is actually reachable rather than discarded.
- `tests/unit/deploy/kubernetes-manifest-generator.test.ts` — 13 cases: generation invariants, target profiles, storage-class semantics, and parity between the generator and `deploy/kubernetes/base`.
- `tests/unit/deploy/kubernetes-provision-plan.test.ts` — 19 cases: the provisioning plan's correctness (including `--tls-san` and the kubeconfig rewrite), the deploy-spec guard rails, and the five review findings below.
- `tests/unit/deploy/kubernetes-cli-command.test.ts` — 10 cases driving the real binary: the stdout contract, exit codes, and argument rejection.

## Coverage Notes

New production code is `src/lib/deploy/kubernetes/` (three pure modules, 830 lines) and `bin/cli/commands/deploy.mjs` (250 lines).

The generator and the spec schema are pure — no cluster, no filesystem, no clock — and are covered directly by the two unit suites. The CLI is covered end to end by a suite that executes `bin/omniroute.mjs` and parses its stdout, which is what pinned the stdout-pollution bug; a mocked test would not have caught it. `bin/omniroute.mjs` gains one condition, exercised by that same suite.

Nothing existing loses coverage. Beyond the new files, the only changes are the two ConfigMap/protocol fixes, that one condition, a `.prettierignore` entry for Helm's Go templates (which Prettier's YAML parser cannot read), and two doc cross-references.

## Reviewer Notes

- **The chart's guard rails live in a `define` that `deployment.yaml` includes.** Helm parses and then discards top-level code in a `_*.tpl` file, so a bare `fail` there is a silent no-op — the first version of this had exactly that bug, and `replicaCount=2` rendered happily. A test now pins the `include`.
- **`storageClassName` is omitted, never set to `""`.** An empty string disables dynamic provisioning entirely; omitting the key binds the cluster default. The two look interchangeable, so a test covers the distinction.
- **The k3s overlay assumes the Traefik that k3s ships by default.** A cluster installed with `--disable=traefik` has no such IngressClass, and the API server accepts the Ingress anyway — it is created and routes nothing. Documented in troubleshooting rather than worked around, since the fix is to name the class the cluster actually runs.
- **Context names accept `:` and `/`.** Managed clusters produce them (an EKS context is `arn:aws:eks:<region>:<account>:cluster/<name>`). Safe because nothing here goes through a shell, the leading-alphanumeric requirement prevents a value being read as an *option*, and — the part that had to change for this to hold — the temp filename in the fetch-kubeconfig step is fixed rather than derived from the context, so a `/` cannot turn it into a path.
- **Recreate means every upgrade is a short full outage** — in-flight SSE and dashboard sessions drop, and the empty-endpoint window returns a controller `502`. That is the SQLite topology, not a probe misconfiguration, and the guide says so where an operator will hit it.
- The `--tls-san` step matters more than it looks: omit it and the cluster works perfectly from the VPS itself while every remote `kubectl` fails TLS verification, which is a confusing way to lose an afternoon.
- No migration, no feature flag, no change to the request path, no new environment variable.

title: fix(claude): claude-fable-5-max returns an empty stream past ~1800 messages when stream=true
body:
Split out of #12334 so that PR #12340 (`Closes #12334`) does not bury a second, unrelated defect.

Reported by @Kizuno18 in #12334, who explicitly offered to separate it — thank you.

## Symptom

`claude-fable-5-max` returns an **empty stream** once the conversation grows beyond roughly 1800 messages. The request does not error; it completes with no content.

## Scope

- Reproduces only with `stream: true`. The same request with `stream: false` is unaffected.
- Unrelated to the combo/priority-advance defect tracked in #12334 (that one is about `hasPerModelQuota()` not listing `claude`, so a model-level failure gets attributed to the connection).

## What is needed

A repro at the message-count boundary, then a root-cause pass on the Claude streaming path — most likely a truncation or buffer limit that silently yields zero events rather than surfacing an upstream error.

Refs #12334

title: feat: orchestration canvas polish (fase 2 PR-A final-review minors)

body:
Itens OK-to-defer da review final whole-branch da PR-A da Fase 2 do Orchestration Canvas (`/dashboard/orchestration`). Nenhum é bloqueante; agrupados para rastreio antes de PR-B1 mudar a cadência de polling.

Manter o `staleSince` anterior quando a fonte já estava falhando.

title: fix(sse): stop mergeAbortSignals from leaking abort listeners
body:
## Summary

`mergeAbortSignals()` in `open-sse/executors/base.ts` attached `"abort"` listeners to its `primary`/`secondary` signals but never removed them once the merged signal settled. Every executor fetch attempt calls this (`fetchWithStartTimeout`, once per URL/retry), so a busy combo request accumulated one live listener per call on the long-lived combo/client signal. A leaked listener still fires when that signal is later aborted (e.g. a hedge cancellation arriving after this merge's own caller already finished), for a merged output nothing is watching anymore.

Fix mirrors the already-correct self-cleaning pattern in `open-sse/utils/directResponseStartTimeout.ts`'s local `mergeAbortSignals`.

Originally investigated from a production crash: `Error [AbortError]: hedge-cancelled` thrown unhandled from deep inside the built Next.js server bundle, killing the whole Node process. This fix addresses one confirmed, measured listener leak on the exact signal-merge path that carries the hedge-cancellation reason through every provider fetch — it removes a real defect regardless, though it was not possible to build a full end-to-end repro of that exact crash through the entire combo-hedging dispatch path.

## Test plan

- [x] TDD: added a regression test (`tests/unit/executor-base-utils.test.ts`) that merges the same long-lived signal 25 times and counts real listener growth via `node:events`' `getEventListeners`.
- [x] Confirmed red on pre-fix code: exactly 25 leaked listeners after 25 merges.
- [x] Confirmed green on fixed code: 0 leaked listeners, 23/23 tests passing in the full file.
- [x] Ran `tests/unit/executor-base-utils.test.ts` on Windows (the platform the original crash was observed on) — 23/23 pass.
- [x] Scoped ESLint on both changed files — 0 new violations (pre-existing violations elsewhere in `base.ts` are outside this diff's hunks).

title: fix(memory): word/sentence-boundary aware fact truncation
body:
## Bug

`src/lib/memory/extraction.ts` truncates extracted memory facts with raw
character-offset slicing and no boundary awareness:

- `sanitizeMatch()` did `raw.trim().replace(/\s+/g, ' ').slice(0, MAX_FACT_LENGTH)`
  — a hard cut that can land mid-word.
- `capExtractionText()` did `text.slice(-MAX_EXTRACTION_TEXT_LENGTH)` on the
  front edge when input exceeds `MAX_EXTRACTION_TEXT_LENGTH` (64KB) — same
  problem, opposite edge.

These facts later get injected into LLM context as `<system-reminder>`
memory blocks, so a mid-word/mid-clause cut produces garbled fragments
(e.g. text starting with a stray closing parenthesis, or ending with no
punctuation and a half word).

## Fix

- `sanitizeMatch()` now backs the cut index off to the nearest clean
  boundary within a lookback window: prefers a sentence-ending mark
  (`.`/`!`/`?`) so the fact reads as a complete clause, falls back to a
  plain whitespace/word boundary, and only falls back to the original hard
  cut when no boundary exists in the window (e.g. one long unbroken run of
  characters).
- `capExtractionText()` applies the equivalent boundary-aware trim on the
  front edge of the kept tail (extends the cut forward to the next
  whitespace boundary rather than slicing mid-word).

This mirrors the boundary-aware truncation already used by
`open-sse/services/compression/lite.ts` (issue #8169) for tool-result
truncation, so the codebase now has one consistent pattern for this class
of problem.

## Testing

- New: `tests/unit/memory-extraction-boundary-truncation.test.ts` — covers
  a long match cut at a word boundary, a match cut preferentially at
  sentence-ending punctuation, short strings passing through untouched,
  the no-boundary-in-window fallback, and `capExtractionText`'s
  boundary-aware tail behavior (both under and over the 64KB cap).
- Ran existing `tests/unit/memory-extraction.test.ts` alongside the new
  file — all 28 tests pass, no regressions:
  ```
  ℹ tests 28
  ℹ pass 28
  ℹ fail 0
  ```
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` — no new type errors introduced by
  this change.

No unrelated files were touched.

title: fix(sse): stop CircuitBreaker.execute() from counting a resolved upstream failure as a success
body:
⚠️ base-red inherited: #12335

## Summary

Fixes #12254. `CircuitBreaker.execute()` calls `_onSuccess()` for any non-throwing resolution of
`fn()`, but `handleChatCore()` returns `{success:false, status:5xx}` for ordinary upstream failures
without throwing. `executeChatWithBreaker`'s `breaker.execute(chatFn)` therefore called
`_onSuccess()` on every dispatch through this call site regardless of outcome — and in CLOSED
state `_onSuccess()` does `failureCount = Math.max(0, failureCount - 1)`, which silently cancelled
the very next explicit `_onFailure()` call in `chat.ts` / `accountFallback.ts` for the same
attempt. `failureCount` could never climb past ~1, so the provider breaker could never open under
sustained genuine failures — on both the direct dispatch path and the combo path (same
per-provider breaker singleton via `getCircuitBreaker(provider)`).

## Fix

Adds `CircuitBreaker.executeTrackingFailureOnly()`: identical `OPEN`/`HALF_OPEN` gating and
identical `isFailure`/`classifyError`-based failure accounting on an actual throw, but it never
calls `_onSuccess()` just because `fn()` resolved. Success/failure accounting for a *resolved*
result stays exactly where it already lives — the explicit `_onSuccess()`/`_onFailure()` call
sites in `chat.ts` and `recordProviderSuccess()`/`recordProviderFailure()` in
`accountFallback.ts` (the combo path already uses these explicitly, per `combo.ts:2358/1870/3587`
gated by `shouldRecordProviderBreakerFailure()`). `executeChatWithBreaker`'s two
`breaker.execute()` call sites are switched to the new method. `CircuitBreaker.execute()` itself
is untouched — it has no other callers in the codebase.

This is the direction discussed in #12254: a shared classification
(`PROVIDER_BREAKER_FAILURE_STATUSES` / `shouldRecordProviderBreakerFailure`) already exists on the
combo side and the single-model side already does explicit `_onFailure()`/`_onSuccess()` calls —
the one remaining gap was this single `execute()` call site quietly fighting all of that explicit
accounting.

## Tests

- `tests/unit/circuit-breaker-provider-accounting-12254.test.ts` — unit tests on `CircuitBreaker`
  directly: no implicit accounting on a resolved (non-throwing) call; failure accounting on an
  actual throw still honors `classifyError`; consecutive genuine failures escalate to `OPEN`
  without being cancelled by interleaved non-throwing calls (the exact reported bug shape); `OPEN`
  and `HALF_OPEN` gating unchanged.
- `tests/unit/execute-chat-with-breaker-accounting-12254.test.ts` — end-to-end reproduction at the
  actual regressed call site: drives 6 real upstream 502s through `executeChatWithBreaker` (mocked
  `global.fetch`, same harness pattern as `execute-chat-resource-pressure-breaker.test.ts`) and
  asserts the breaker accumulates zero implicit accounting.

Ran locally: `npm run typecheck:core` (clean), `npm run lint` (clean), `npm run check:cycles`
(clean), plus the full existing circuit-breaker/combo-provider-cooldown/account-fallback test
files (174 tests, all passing) to confirm no regression from the new method or the two swapped
call sites.

## Changelog

Fragment to follow in this same branch once the PR number is known (`changelog.d/README.md`
convention).

title: fix(models): publish effort_tiers on base model for kimi/codex/glm providers
body:
## Summary

`GET /v1/models` did not advertise Kimi K3's reasoning-effort vocabulary (`low`/`high`/`max`) on `kmca/k3` or `kmca/k3-256k`, even though the synced metadata contained `supportedThinkingEfforts: ["low", "high", "max"]`. Catalog-only clients (OpenCode, plain SDK pickers) had no tiers to copy and fell back to inventing incorrect values.

Root cause: `effectiveEffortTiers()` in `syncedCapabilities.ts` called `isSkippedEffortProvider(ownedBy)` which returned `true` for any kimi-prefixed provider, immediately returning `undefined` and suppressing effort_tiers on the base model. The `isSkippedEffortProvider` gate was designed to prevent synthetic `<id>-<tier>` variant generation (in `shouldExposeSyncedEffortVariants`), not to suppress base-model tier visibility.

Fix: remove the `isSkippedEffortProvider` check from `effectiveEffortTiers()` so the base model publishes its tiers. The synthetic variant prevention in `shouldExposeSyncedEffortVariants` remains unchanged.

## Related Issues

- Closes #12299

## Validation

- [x] Change type: models/catalog
- [x] All 47 related tests pass across 3 test files
- [x] Pre-commit hooks passed (Prettier, ESLint, docs-sync, any-budget, tracked-artifacts)

## Tests Added Or Updated

- **Updated**: `tests/unit/synced-capabilities-learned-effort-override.test.ts` - changed 12 tests to assert excluded providers DO publish effort_tiers on base model
- **Added**: `tests/unit/kimi-k3-effort-tiers-12299.test.ts` - 6 tests covering kimi K3/K3-256k effort_tiers, merge path, synthetic variant prevention, and static registry verification

## Reviewer Notes

- This is a semantic fix: the isSkippedEffortProvider gate has two purposes (1) preventing synthetic variant generation and (2) suppressing base-model tier visibility. Only (2) was incorrect.
- The changelog fragment uses 0000 as placeholder PR number.

title: fix(providers): Codex Responses + Gemini 3 Flash loops on narrated tool intent instead of emitting function_call
body:
### OmniRoute Version

3.8.50

### Installation Method

npm (global)

### Operating System

Windows

### OS Version

Windows 11

### Node.js Version

v24.7.0

### Provider(s) Involved

Gemini (direct Gemini provider)

### Model(s) Involved

`gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview`

### Client Tool

OpenAI Codex CLI

### Description

When Codex CLI uses `gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview` through OmniRoute's `/v1/responses` endpoint, agentic tool use can get stuck in a loop.

Gemini appears to understand that a local tool should be used, but instead of returning a structured function/tool call to Codex, it repeatedly outputs plain text describing the action it intends to perform.

Example:

> I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
>
> I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
>
> I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.

No local filesystem/tool action is executed, and Codex continues repeating the same intention until the request is manually aborted.

Gemini 3 Flash supports native function calling, so this appears to be an interoperability issue in the **Codex Responses API → OmniRoute → Gemini tool-calling path**, rather than a missing model capability.

This may be related to PR #8211, which already documents Gemini Flash models sometimes narrating an intended tool call as text instead of emitting a real `functionCall`.

However, #8211 mainly added support for mapping `tool_choice: "required"` to Gemini `ANY`. Normal Codex agent requests use `tool_choice: "auto"`, which OmniRoute maps to Gemini `VALIDATED`, so the problem can still occur during normal Codex usage.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure Codex CLI to use OmniRoute via the Responses API:

```toml
wire_api = "responses"
base_url = "http://localhost:20128/v1"
```

2. Configure a model or combo whose selected target is:

```text
gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview
```

3. Open Codex in a normal coding workspace where local tools such as filesystem and shell access are available.

4. Use a project containing instructions that cause Codex to inspect the workspace, for example an `AGENTS.md` file or similar project instructions.

5. Send a simple request such as:

```text
ping
```

6. Codex decides that it should inspect the workspace, for example the `memory-bank/` directory.

7. Observe that instead of executing the filesystem tool, the assistant repeatedly prints statements such as:

> I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.

8. The loop continues until the request is manually aborted.

### Expected Behavior

When Gemini decides that a local Codex tool is required, OmniRoute should preserve the structured tool-call round trip:

```text
Codex /v1/responses
  → OmniRoute
  → Gemini functionCall
  → OmniRoute
  → OpenAI Responses function_call
  → Codex executes local tool
  → function_call_output
  → model continues
```

Codex should execute the requested filesystem/shell operation and continue the task normally.

### Actual Behavior

Instead of emitting an executable tool call, the model repeatedly narrates the action it intends to perform:

```text
I'll start by exploring the workspace and checking the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the current state of the project.
I'll start by exploring the workspace and checking the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the current state of the project.
I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
```

No local tool execution occurred, and the request had to be manually aborted.

### Test Impact

Needs a new integration test

### Error Logs / Output

There was no HTTP error. OmniRoute reported a successful Gemini request.

Relevant OmniRoute call-log information:

```text
POST /v1/responses
status: 200
provider: gemini
model: gemini-3-flash-preview
requestedModel: gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview
sourceFormat: openai-responses
targetFormat: gemini
duration: ~28s
error: null
```

Codex output before manually aborting:

```text
I'll start by exploring the workspace and checking the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the current state of the project.
I'll start by exploring the workspace and checking the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the current state of the project.
I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
I'll list the contents of the `memory-bank/` directory to understand the project's current state.
```

The exported OmniRoute call log omitted the complete request and response bodies due to the payload size limit. Therefore, I cannot currently confirm whether Gemini emitted no `functionCall` at all, or whether a structured call was lost during translation back to the OpenAI Responses format.

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Additional Context

OmniRoute is running locally on Windows:

```text
http://localhost:20128
```

Codex uses the OpenAI Responses API through OmniRoute:

```toml
wire_api = "responses"
```

The request was routed through a small priority combo. Gemini was the first target and was selected immediately, so this reproduction did not involve cascading through multiple providers.

Relevant routing order:

```text
1. gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview
2. groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b
3. openrouter/qwen/qwen3-coder
```

No fallback occurred because the Gemini request itself returned HTTP 200.

This appears related to PR #8211:

> `fix(sse): Gemini malformed function-call handling + tool_choice translation`

That PR documents a Gemini Flash model being observed to:

> narrate an intended tool call in plain text instead of actually emitting one

The current OmniRoute Gemini translator maps:

```text
tool_choice unset/auto    → VALIDATED
tool_choice required/any  → ANY
tool_choice none          → NONE
specific function         → ANY + allowedFunctionNames
```

Codex normally sends:

```text
tool_choice: "auto"
```

Therefore, the `required → ANY` fix does not cover the normal Codex agent path.

I do not think simply changing all `auto` requests to Gemini `ANY` would be correct, because that would change the semantics of `auto` and force a tool call even when one is unnecessary.

The suspected path is therefore:

```text
Codex /v1/responses
  tool_choice: auto
        ↓
OmniRoute Responses → Chat normalization
        ↓
OpenAI → Gemini translation
  auto → VALIDATED
        ↓
Gemini may narrate intended tool usage as prose
        ↓
Codex receives no executable tool call
        ↓
Agent can repeat the same intended action
```

This is only a suspected explanation. The raw upstream Gemini response was not available in the exported call log, so it is not yet proven whether the `functionCall` is missing at the Gemini side or lost later during response translation.

### Validation Plan

At minimum, a targeted integration test should verify the complete **Codex/OpenAI Responses → Gemini → OpenAI Responses** tool-call round trip.

Existing tests around PR #8211 should remain green, especially:

```bash
node --import tsx --test tests/unit/gemini-tool-choice.test.ts
```

A new regression test should be added for the Codex Responses API path, for example:

```bash
node --import tsx --test tests/integration/gemini-codex-responses-tool-call.test.ts
```

The new test should exercise:

```text
/v1/responses
tool_choice = auto
function tools present
Gemini native functionCall
Responses function_call returned to client
function_call_output accepted
successful continuation
```

The test should verify that:

1. Responses API function tools survive the Responses → Chat → Gemini translation.
2. Gemini receives valid `functionDeclarations`.
3. A native Gemini `functionCall` is translated back into an OpenAI Responses `function_call`.
4. The function name, call ID, and arguments are preserved.
5. A subsequent `function_call_output` can be sent back successfully.
6. The model continues after the tool result instead of repeatedly narrating the intended action.

It is important that the regression test uses:

```text
tool_choice: "auto"
```

and not only:

```text
tool_choice: "required"
```

because `auto` represents the normal Codex agent path involved in this reproduction.

The general project checks should also remain green:

```bash
npm run test:unit
npm run test:integration
npm run check
```

For live verification, running Codex CLI through OmniRoute with `gemini/gemini-3-flash-preview` and repeating the reproduction above should result in a real local tool execution instead of repeated prose describing the intended action.

title: fix(cli): remove duplicate positional argument in tunnel create command
body:
## Summary

`omniroute tunnel create <type>` crashed immediately with `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading optsWithGlobals)` because Commander.js registered two positional arguments for `type`.

The subcommand was declared as `.command("create [type]")` and then `.addArgument(new Argument("[type]", ...))` was called, which added a second `type` positional. Commander passed four arguments `(type, type2, opts, command)` to the action callback, but the handler destructured only three `(type, opts, cmd)` — so `cmd` was bound to the real opts object and `cmd.parent` was `undefined`.

Fix: change `.command("create [type]")` to `.command("create")` and rely solely on `.addArgument()` for the optional type argument with choices and default — matching how the other subcommands (`stop`, `status`, `logs`, `info`, `rotate`) each declare a single positional.

## Related Issues

- Closes #12295

## Validation

- [x] Change type: CLI
- [x] Focused tests: `node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/cli-tunnel-create-command.test.ts` — 3/3 pass
- [x] Existing tunnel tests pass: `tests/unit/tunnel-routes-error-sanitization.test.ts` (9/9) and `tests/unit/authz/route-guard-tunnel-processes-local-only.test.ts` (4/4)
- [x] Pre-commit hooks passed (Prettier, ESLint, docs-sync, any-budget, tracked-artifacts)
- [x] TypeScript typecheck passes

## Tests Added Or Updated

Specs from the official docs: 1M context, 128K max output, adaptive-only thinking (cannot be disabled), non-default `temperature`/`top_p`/`top_k` rejected with a 400, $10/$50 per MTok — same list price as Fable 5, but **cache reads at $0.25/MTok** (a quarter of Fable 5's read price).

## Where it's added

Mirrors the existing `claude-fable-5` entries, only on surfaces that actually serve the model today:

- **Provider registries**: `anthropic` (API key), `claude` (OAuth), `claude/web`, `vertex` (Google Cloud lists `claude-fable-5-1` natively)
- **modelSpecs**: capabilities (`rejectsThinkingDisabled`, `adaptiveThinkingOnly`) + Bedrock aliases (`anthropic.claude-fable-5-1` per official docs)
- **Pricing**: new `CLAUDE_FABLE_5_1_PRICING` shared tier (frontier-labs) and the `cc` OAuth subscription table — both with the $0.25 cache-read price; `providerCostData` row
- **`CONTEXT_1M_SUPPORTED_MODELS`**, `staticModels` (claude), `modelFamilyFallback` (falls to `claude-fable-5`, then `claude-opus-5`/`claude-sonnet-5`)

## Deliberately not added

- Third-party gateway registries (cursor, kiro, github-copilot, etc.): their upstream catalogs haven't published the model — adding it there would be speculative.
- Fast-mode default list: fast-mode availability for 5.1 is not documented.

## Verification

- `typecheck:core` clean
- Catalog/pricing/context-1m/family-fallback/sampling-params test suites: 35/35 pass (`catalog-updates-v3x`, `claude-context-1m-supported-models`, `model-family-fallback-notation`, `catalog-pricing-lookup-index-8697`, `claude-adaptive-sampling-params`, `cc-discovery-aliases-catalog`)
- Pre-commit hooks (prettier, eslint with project suppressions, docs-sync, any-budget) pass

title: fix(providers): stop an unrelated-provider tiktoken bundling failure from crashing /api/providers
body:
## Summary

`/api/providers` (and every barrel importer of `@/lib/providers/validation`) 500'd on every single request, caused by an unrelated provider's WASM tokenizer failing to bundle under Turbopack dev mode. Traced live: this cascaded into the combos dashboard appearing to have zero combos despite `context_handoffs`... er, `/api/combos` genuinely returning the right data every time.

## What was actually happening

1. `src/app/api/providers/route.ts` statically imports `finalizeValidatedChatGptWebCodexSecrets` from `chatgptWebCodexAdmin.ts` at module scope, even though it's only used inside the one `provider === "chatgpt-web-codex"` branch.
2. That module's transitive chain (vendor ChatGPT-Web browser adapter → `token-estimate.ts` → `tiktoken`'s WASM tokenizer) fails to bundle under Turbopack dev mode -- even with `tiktoken` already listed in `serverExternalPackages` (confirmed: the standalone Node `require()` works fine; only Turbopack's bundling of this specific import graph doesn't).
3. A static import evaluates that whole chain on **every** request regardless of which provider is actually being managed, turning an unrelated provider's bundling bug into a route-wide 500 for everyone.
4. Found the same pattern one layer deeper: `validation/chatgptWebCodex.ts` (a per-provider validator re-exported through the shared `@/lib/providers/validation` barrel that every provider validator's callers pull in) also statically imports `detectChromeExecutable` from the same `executors/chatgpt-web-codex.ts` module -- crashing anyone who merely imports the barrel, including code with nothing to do with chatgpt-web-codex.

**Observed cascading effect:** the combos dashboard page's `fetchData()` awaits four parallel requests (`combos`, `providers`, `combos/metrics`, `provider-nodes`) sequentially and calls `.json()` on each *before* ever calling `setCombos()`. Next.js dev mode returns an HTML error page (not JSON) for an uncaught exception, so `/api/providers`'s 500 threw inside that sequence and aborted the whole function before the combos fetch's own successful response was ever applied to state -- even though `/api/combos` itself returned `200` with the correct single combo every single time it was called standalone.

**Also fixes a related, independently-discovered SSR/hydration bug** in the same page: `showUsageGuide`'s `useState` lazy initializer read `localStorage` directly. SSR has no `localStorage`, so the server always computed "not dismissed" while the client could compute a different real value -- a hydration mismatch that forces React to discard and remount the client tree in dev mode, which could interrupt the fetch effect's in-flight state update. Moved the read into a mount effect instead.

## Fix

Made both `chatgptWebCodexAdmin.ts` and `executors/chatgpt-web-codex.ts` imports dynamic (`await import(...)`), loaded only when the `chatgpt-web-codex` branch actually runs, at both call sites. No behavior change to the validation logic itself.

## User Impact

- `/api/providers` (and anything importing the shared validation barrel) no longer crashes because of an unrelated provider's bundling issue.
- The combos dashboard reliably shows existing combos again.
- The `showUsageGuide` SSR/hydration mismatch is gone.

## Validation

- [x] Live-verified on a real deployment: root-caused via `call_logs`/server logs, applied the fix, confirmed `/api/providers` returns `200` and the combos page shows the existing combo again after a full restart.
- [x] `tests/unit/chatgpt-web-codex.test.ts`, `tests/unit/providers-route-codex-account-pool.test.ts`, `tests/unit/providers-route-managed-catalog.test.ts`, `tests/unit/providers-route-model-autofetch-optin.test.ts`, `tests/unit/providers-route-patch-method.test.ts`, `tests/unit/provider-journey.contract.test.ts` -- 50/50 pass.
- [x] Complexity ratchet: no new violations.
- [x] Reconciled with `upstream/release/v3.8.51` tip at branch time.

title: fix(api): preserve API key ACL on creation
body:
## Summary

Fixes #12275 by preserving explicit API-key ACL fields during `POST /api/keys` creation instead of silently falling back to permissive defaults.

## Problem

A create request could include:

- `modelAccessMode: "restricted"`
- `allowedModels`
- `allowedCombos`

but the creation path did not preserve those fields. The key was created with broader defaults (`modelAccessMode='all'`, empty model list interpreted as allow-all, and `allowedCombos=['combo/*']`).

Security invariant:

> Requested restriction must not result in broader effective authorization.

## Root Cause

- `createKeySchema` did not include the ACL fields, so validation stripped them.
- `POST /api/keys` did not destructure or forward them.
- `createApiKey()` only accepted `allowedConnections` in creation options and inserted permissive ACL defaults.

## Solution

- Add create-path schema support for `modelAccessMode`, `allowedModels`, and `allowedCombos`.
- Forward validated ACL fields from `POST /api/keys` into `createApiKey()`.
- Extend `createApiKey()` options and persist ACL fields in the initial insert, avoiding a create-then-update fail-open window.
- Return created ACL fields in the 201 response for readback evidence.
- Add an integration regression test that checks response, persisted state, model enforcement, and combo enforcement.

## Validation

Passed:

```bash
node --import tsx/esm --test tests/integration/api-keys.test.ts
# 17 pass, 0 fail

npm run typecheck:core
# pass

git diff --check
# pass
```

Regression proof:

- With the new regression test present and the source fix reverted, the test failed on the create-path ACL readback: actual `undefined`, expected `restricted`.
- Restoring the fix made the same focused integration test pass.

Not fully green locally:

```bash
npm run lint
```

failed on the current repository baseline with 5161 errors across 1053 files, mostly pre-existing `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` and `@typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars` reports. I did not change lint policy or suppress failures.

## Scope / Risk

In scope:

- API-key creation schema/handler/persistence
- focused regression coverage for #12275

Out of scope:

- broad authorization engine refactor
- WebSocket authorization
- other credential types
- provider-plugin or marketplace governance changes

Compatibility:

- Requests that omit ACL fields keep the existing defaults.
- Explicit restricted requests now preserve and enforce the requested narrower policy.

## Effective Authorization Proof

This regression verifies authorization behavior, not only persistence/readback.

REQUESTED:
- restricted
- allowedModels = ["openai/gpt-4.1-mini"]
- allowedCombos = ["focused-chat"]

PERSISTED:
- restricted
- ["openai/gpt-4.1-mini"]
- ["focused-chat"]

EFFECTIVE AUTHORIZATION:

| Target | Requested | Effective |
|---|---|---|
| openai/gpt-4.1-mini | allow | ALLOW |
| anthropic/claude-4-5 | deny | DENY |
| focused-chat | allow | ALLOW |
| blocked-chat | deny | DENY |

## Effective Behavior

- `getApiKeyById` returns exactly the requested ACL shape.
- `validateApiKey` allows the requested model/combo and denies unlisted targets.

No broader effective authorization is produced from the creation path.

title: fix(ci): openapi-security-tiers checker honors routeGuard patterns + imported prefixes (base-red #12335)
body:
## Summary

Fixes one of the two reproducible hard failures behind **base-red #12335** on `release/v3.8.51`: `npm run check:openapi-security-tiers` reported **13 false "not covered" failures** and blocked the branch.

**This is a checker bug, not a security hole — the routes were never open.** `routeGuard.isLocalOnlyPath()` classifies a loopback-only route through **two** mechanisms, but the static checker only understood one:

| Mechanism | Example route | Checker saw it? |
|---|---|---|
| `LOCAL_ONLY_API_PREFIXES` (string literals) | `/api/mcp/` | ✅ |
| `LOCAL_ONLY_API_PREFIXES` **imported const** `VNC_ROUTE_PREFIX` | `/api/vnc-session/*` | ❌ (saw literal token `VNC_ROUTE_PREFIX`) |
| `LOCAL_ONLY_API_PATTERNS` (regex) | `/api/providers/{id}/login`, `volcengine-plan/connect*`, `refresh-cursor`, `chatgpt-web-codex-doctor` | ❌ (never read) |

PR #12212 (documented 276→692 routes) added `x-loopback-only: true` to those pattern-/const-covered routes, which the text-scraping checker couldn't see → 13 spurious failures.

## Proof it's the checker, not the code

I called the real `isLocalOnlyPath()` on every one of the 13 flagged routes (params substituted): **all 13 return `true`** (protected), and the negative control `/v1/chat/completions` returns `false`. The enforcement is correct; only the gate was stale. `routeGuard.ts` is **unchanged**.

## The fix (checker only)

`scripts/check/check-openapi-security-tiers.mjs` now mirrors the `isLocalOnlyPath()` contract (covered = prefix **OR** pattern):
- Extracts each array up to `\n];` instead of `[^\]]+` — immune to `]` inside comments or regex char classes like `[^/]` (the footgun the routeGuard `cursor/auto-import` comment already documents, and the reason the pattern array couldn't be parsed at all).
- Resolves bare-identifier prefixes (`VNC_ROUTE_PREFIX`) by following their import to the string literal — generic, so future imported prefixes work too.
- Evaluates `LOCAL_ONLY_API_PATTERNS`, concretizing OpenAPI `{param}` templates so they match the `[^/]+` regexes.

## Test plan
- `npm run check:openapi-security-tiers` → **PASS** (was FAIL/exit 1 with 13 errors).
- Detection preserved: parses 42 prefixes (VNC resolved to `/api/vnc-session`) + 4 patterns; a bogus `x-loopback-only` route matching neither still returns `false` → would still fail the gate.
- The remaining `traffic-inspector/sessions*` lines are the **non-fatal WARN** pass (pre-existing annotation gaps the checker deliberately keeps non-blocking); they do not fail the gate.
- Scripts-only change (`scripts/check/`), no production code touched.

## Scope
Deliberately narrow — this greens the gate. The pre-existing non-fatal annotation warnings (`/api/tools/traffic-inspector/*` missing `x-loopback-only`) are a separate doc-only follow-up.

> Part of clearing base-red **#12335**. Companion PR fixes the other reproducible failure (eslint dead-code in `stream-passthrough-usage-estimation.test.ts`).

title: feat(providers): add Claude Fable 5.1 support
body:
## Summary

Wires `claude-fable-5-1` (Claude Fable 5.1) across the full first-party model pipeline so it is a first-class, routable model in OmniRoute — mirroring the original Fable 5 rollout (#3524), adapted to the current (refactored, per-provider) registry layout.

Fable 5.1 shares Fable 5's profile: 1M context, 128k output, adaptive-only thinking (rejects `thinking.type:"disabled"`, #3554), vision + tools. It is listed **first** in every Claude catalog, so it becomes the default resolved Fable tier (`ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_FABLE_MODEL`).

**Also bumps the pinned Claude Code wire identity from `2.1.220` to `2.1.258`.** Anthropic gates Fable 5.1 behind Claude Code ≥ 2.1.251, so with the old fingerprint every `claude-fable-5-1` request over the native Claude OAuth path (built-in catalog entry or custom model alike) was rejected upstream before the model was even considered:

```
[400]: Claude Code 2.1.220 does not support this model; version 2.1.251 or newer is required. Run 'claude update', or update the Claude desktop app, then try again.
```

## What changed

**Core pipeline**
- **Model spec** (`src/shared/constants/modelSpecs.ts`) — 1M ctx / 128k out, `adaptiveThinkingOnly`, `rejectsThinkingDisabled`, Bedrock aliases.
- **Pricing** — `CLAUDE_FABLE_5_1_PRICING` (`shared-tiers.ts`), native Anthropic rate `$15/$75` (`frontier-labs.ts`), cc OAuth rate `$10/$50` (`oauth-subscriptions.ts`), token-cost table (`providerCostData.ts`).
- **Fallback chain** (`modelFamilyFallback.ts`) — `claude-fable-5-1 → claude-fable-5 → claude-opus-4-8 → claude-opus-4-7 → claude-sonnet-5` (degrades to the previous Fable tier first).
- **1M-context beta** (`context1m.ts`), **fast mode** (`claudeFastMode.ts` + `settings.ts` default), **static models** (`staticModels.ts`).

**First-party provider registries** — `cc`/`claude`, `claude-web`, `anthropic`, `vertex`, `vertex-partner`, `ghe-copilot`, `github`. In each, 5.1 is placed above 5 (newest-first), which is what makes `getClaudeCodeDefaultModels()` resolve 5.1 as the default.

**Claude Code wire identity (prerequisite for Fable 5.1 to be served)**
- **Canonical constant** (`src/shared/constants/claudeCodeClient.ts`) — the single leaf that feeds the `User-Agent`, the `x-anthropic-billing-header` system block and the `X-Stainless-*` headers on the Claude OAuth executor, the CC-compatible relay path and the CC bridge transforms:

  | Field | Before | After |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | `CLAUDE_CODE_CLIENT_VERSION` | `2.1.220` | `2.1.258` |
  | `CLAUDE_CODE_CLIENT_BUILD_REVISION` | `1f2` | `1e2` |
  | `CLAUDE_CODE_SDK_PACKAGE_VERSION` (`X-Stainless-Package-Version`) | `0.94.0` | `0.112.1` |
  | `CLAUDE_CODE_RUNTIME_VERSION` (`X-Stainless-Runtime-Version`) | `v26.3.0` | `v26.3.0` (unchanged — Bun 1.4.1 still reports it) |

- **Capture method** — wire-exact, not guessed: the signed Claude Code `2.1.258` binary was pointed at a loopback listener via `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` and the headers + `system[0]` of its `/v1/messages?beta=true` request were recorded (`claude-cli/2.1.258 (external, sdk-cli)`, `x-stainless-package-version: 0.112.1`, `x-stainless-runtime-version: v26.3.0`, `cc_version=2.1.258.1e2`). Note the real CLI derives the 3-char billing suffix from the prompt (a second prompt produced `33b`); OmniRoute already models it as a captured static value, so `1e2` follows the existing convention.
- **Dashboard routing preset** (`RoutingTab.tsx`) — `inject_billing_header.buildRevision` now imports `CLAUDE_CODE_CLIENT_BUILD_REVISION` instead of hardcoding `"1f2"`, so the UI mirror can no longer drift from the server default on the next bump.
- **Docs / examples refreshed to the new fingerprint** — `docs/security/STEALTH_GUIDE.md`, `docs/reference/ENVIRONMENT.md`, `docs/providers/AGENTROUTER.md`, and the active `CLAUDE_USER_AGENT` line in `.env.example` (it still said `2.1.219`; a fresh `.env` generated from the example would have pinned the old User-Agent and reproduced the 400 even after the code bump).
- **Not touched** — the Devin bridge image (`docker/devin-bridge/`) installs a *real* Claude Code `2.1.220`; Fable 5.1 through that bridge needs its own version bump in a follow-up.

**Deliberately excluded**
- **Kiro** — its upstream serves no Fable tier; the fabricated ids were removed after live VPS validation (#6170). A regression test keeps it out.
- **Third-party aggregators** (cursor, blackbox, kie, opencode-zen, cheaperinference, freebuff, tinycms, auggie, devin, notion-web) — upstream availability of 5.1 there is unverified; left for a follow-up once confirmed.

**Docs** — CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry; `docs/providers/CLAUDE_WEB.md` catalog row.

## Auto-derived (no code needed)
- **Effort variants** `claude-fable-5-1-{low,medium,high,xhigh}` synthesize automatically from the spec (`supportsThinking`) — verified at runtime.
- GitHub Copilot live discovery + HyperAgent subagent routing already handle 5.1 generically.
