title: fix(api): GET /v1/models hides Kimi K3 effort_tiers (low/high/max)
body:
### OmniRoute Version

3.8.50 (npm global, live server)

### Installation Method

npm (global)

### Operating System

Windows

### OS Version

Windows Server 2022

### Node.js Version

24.x

### Provider(s) Involved

kimi-coding-apikey (kmca)

### Model(s) Involved

k3, k3-256k

### Client Tool

OpenCode (catalog from GET /v1/models)

### Description

GET /v1/models does not advertise Kimi K3's real reasoning-effort vocabulary (low / high / max) on kmca/k3 or kmca/k3-256k.

Catalog-only clients that pull OmniRoute's catalog (OpenCode) therefore have no K3-specific tiers to copy. They fall back to Grok/OpenAI's low / medium / high / xhigh. Official Kimi docs only allow low / high / max.

This is a catalog bug, not a wrong stored word list. Synced metadata already has supportedThinkingEfforts: ["low","high","max"], and runtime.ts has the same list. Those values never reach /v1/models.

Related, not a duplicate: #10788 (opencode/ollama/nvidia catalog), #10003 (k3-256k runtime, closed), #7694 (kimi skip was meant to block synthetic <id>-<tier> suffix IDs, but now also blanks capabilities.effort_tiers on the base model).

Official contract: https://platform.kimi.com/docs/guide/use-reasoning-effort

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Add a kimi-coding-apikey connection that syncs k3 / k3-256k.
2. Confirm synced JSON has supportedThinkingEfforts: ["low","high","max"].
3. GET /v1/models and inspect kmca/k3 and kmca/k3-256k.
4. Compare with ds/deepseek-v4-pro, which does expose effort_tiers.

### Expected Behavior

Base entries kmca/k3 and kmca/k3-256k should expose effort_tiers: ["low","high","max"].
If skipping synthetic kmca/k3-low suffix IDs is still intentional, that skip must not also hide the three tiers on the base model.

### Actual Behavior

Live 3.8.50 catalog returns bare kmca/k3 and kmca/k3-256k with no thinking / effort_tiers. Catalog-only clients invent medium and xhigh for K3.

### Test Impact

Needs a new unit test

### Error Logs / Output

```shell
GET /v1/models (3.8.50):
kmca/k3
kmca/k3-256k
(no thinking / effort_tiers)

ds/deepseek-v4-pro thinking: true + -low/-high/-max aliases

Synced metadata (correct, unpublished): {"id":"k3","supportedThinkingEfforts":["low","high","max"],"defaultThinkingEffort":"high","supportsThinking":true}
```

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Additional Context

Root cause in 3.8.50:
1. Static k3 registry only sets supportsReasoning:true, no supportedThinkingEfforts (list lives in KIMI_CODE_STATIC_THINKING_POLICIES).
2. catalog.ts skipCanonicalEffortFallback when no declared tiers (#9485) -> no effort_tiers.
3. syncedCapabilities.effectiveEffortTiers() calls isSkippedEffortProvider(ownedBy); kimi-coding-apikey matches the kimi prefix, so even a synced low/high/max list is dropped from the BASE entry.

isSkippedEffortProvider is correct for not synthesizing <id>-<tier> aliases. Using it to blank base-model effort_tiers leaves catalog-only clients with nothing to copy.

Fix: keep skipping kmca/k3-low suffix IDs if wanted; still publish effort_tiers: ["low","high","max"] on kmca/k3 and kmca/k3-256k.

### Validation Plan

Unit: buildSyncedCapabilities({id:"k3",supportsThinking:true,supportedThinkingEfforts:["low","high","max"]},"kimi-coding-apikey") includes those tiers; appendSyncedEffortVariants still does not add k3-low.
After fix: GET /v1/models for kmca/k3 shows effort_tiers low/high/max, not medium/xhigh.

title: fix(providers): dashboard shows stale data after deleting custom providers/models until a full page reload
body:
## Environment
- Branch: **`release/v3.8.51`** (latest release branch) @ `073b98462`
- OS: Windows 11, Node **v24.18.0**, dev mode (Turbopack); reported from fork `chirag127/OmniRoute`

## Symptom
After deleting a **custom (OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible) provider** or its models from the dashboard, the UI does not refresh — the deleted provider/model keeps showing until a **manual full page reload**.

Repro (provider level):
1. Add a custom OpenAI-compatible provider, open its detail page (`/dashboard/providers/<id>`).
2. Click **Delete** (header action) → `DELETE /api/provider-nodes/<id>`.
3. The app calls `router.push("/dashboard/providers")`.
4. The Providers list still shows the deleted provider until F5.

## What I verified
- Server-side deletion is correct: I live-tested model delete on a running instance — `POST /api/provider-models` → `GET` shows the model → `DELETE` returns `{"removed":true,...}` → subsequent `GET` no longer contains it. So the stale data is a **client-side refresh gap**, not a broken delete API.

## Suspected root cause (client-side)
1. **Providers list page** — `src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/providers/page.tsx` loads all data exactly once in `useEffect(..., [])` via `loadProviderPageData()` and has **no refetch-on-focus, no polling, no `router.refresh`** hook. Deleting a provider from the detail page (`components/CompatibleNodeCard.tsx`) does `router.push("/dashboard/providers")` **without `router.refresh()`**, so a soft navigation back to the previously-cached list can render the deleted provider.
2. **Provider detail models list** — `ProviderModelsSection` renders from a `models` `useMemo` over `syncedAvailableModels` + `modelMeta.customModels`; after model deletes, `onModelsChanged` → `fetchProviderModelMeta()` refetches both, but the refresh is skipped if any step in the delete chain fails silently (e.g. the alias-delete path in `useProviderModels.handleDeleteAlias`), leaving rows visible.

## Suggested fix
- Call `router.refresh()` after provider-node deletion, and/or make the Providers list page re-fetch on window focus / route refocus (or use a shared invalidation signal).
- In the model-delete chain, always run the list refetch in a `finally`-style path so a failed alias delete can't suppress the models refresh.

title: feat(startup): purge stale Turbopack dev cache when known app routes 404 after a dev-server restart

labels.name: backlog
labels.description: Tracked for future work; not blocking

body:
## Environment
- Branch: **`release/v3.8.51`** (latest release branch, fully synced with upstream) @ `073b98462`
- OS: Windows 11, Node **v24.18.0**, `npm run dev` (Turbopack dev mode)
- Reported from fork `chirag127/OmniRoute`

## Symptom
After the dev server has run once, is stopped, and a new instance is started, a **subset of dashboard routes 404** — while other routes keep working. In our case every `/dashboard/settings/*` sub-route returned 404:

| Route | Result |
|---|---|
| `/dashboard/settings/general` | **404** |
| `/dashboard/settings/security` | **404** |
| `/dashboard/settings/appearance` | **404** |
| `/dashboard/settings/advanced` | **404** |
| `/dashboard/settings` | 200 |
| `/dashboard/providers`, `/dashboard/logs`, `/dashboard` | 200 |

Note: unauthenticated requests to the 404-ing routes **307-redirect to `/login`** (so the route is matched by the auth layout), but after a successful login the same URL returns **404**.

## Root cause
The Turbopack **persistent dev cache** at `.build/next/dev/cache/turbopack` (4.1 GB) was last written at 12:25, while the dev server serving the 404s had started at 17:45 — i.e. a newer server instance read a **stale/corrupted persistent cache**. The main `app-paths-manifest.json` (also from 12:25) *did* contain the settings routes, but per-route compiled artifacts were inconsistent, so route matching partially failed.

**Purging `.build/next/dev/cache/turbopack` and restarting the dev server resolves it completely** — every route returns 200.

## Relation to #6289
This is the same Turbopack persistent-cache corruption class as #6289, but a **different manifestation**: instead of the startup crash (`os error 1455` / misleading "Module not found"), it surfaces as **silent 404s on a subset of routes**. `scripts/dev/turbopackCacheHeal.mjs` only purges on the startup crash signature, so this mode is not detected.

## Repro
1. `npm run dev` (Turbopack), visit several dashboard routes.
2. Stop the server.
3. Start `npm run dev` again.
4. Visit `/dashboard/settings/general` → 404 (even with a valid session).

## Suggested fix
In the dev launcher, detect "known app routes returning 404 at startup" (e.g. compare requested route against the compiled app-paths manifest + source tree) and purge the Turbopack cache, or invalidate the persistent cache when the route manifest is older than the source files it maps.

title: fix(startup): "Invalid regular expression flags" crash right after STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY generation on first run
body:
### Description
A user on the Discord (EN) support channel reported a crash right after first-run bootstrap generates the storage encryption key:

```
omniroute
  📋 Loaded env from /usr/lib/node_modules/omniroute/.env
  ✨ Generated STORAGE_ENCRYPTION_KEY in /root/.omniroute/.env
✖ Invalid regular expression flags
❯ ✖ Invalid regular expression flags
```

`"Invalid regular expression flags"` is a native V8/`SyntaxError` thrown by `new RegExp(pattern, flags)` when constructing a regex with an unsupported/invalid flags string — not a string that exists literally anywhere in this codebase (checked `src/`, `open-sse/`, `bin/`), so this is likely either a transitive dependency behavior triggered by an environment value, or a Node/V8 version mismatch (other reports in the same channel around the same time also involved unsupported Node versions, e.g. v23.7.0 outside the `>=22.22.2 <23 || >=24.0.0 <27` supported range — see `AGENTS.md` → Environment).

### Missing info (needed before this can be worked)
- `node -v` output
- Operating System + OS version
- Full command that was run (npm global install? npx? which package manager?)
- Whether it happens on a fresh `DATA_DIR` every time, or only once

### Status
This is a tracking issue opened from the support mesh pending the reporter's environment details — not yet reproduced locally.

title: fix: omniroute tunnel create <type> crashes with "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading optsWithGlobals)"
body:
### Description
`omniroute tunnel create <type>` (cloudflare/tailscale/ngrok) crashes immediately instead of creating a tunnel. Because tunnel creation never actually starts, follow-up commands like `tunnel status`/`tunnel logs` then return `Error: HTTP 404`.

### Root cause (verified)
`bin/cli/commands/tunnel.mjs:20-30` double-declares the `type` positional argument for the `create` subcommand:

```js
tunnel
  .command("create [type]")                 // declares positional #1 ("type")
  .addArgument(
    new Argument("[type]", "Tunnel type").choices(VALID_TUNNEL_TYPES).default("cloudflare")
  )                                          // declares positional #2 (also "type")
  .action(async (type, opts, cmd) => {
    const globalOpts = cmd.parent.optsWithGlobals();   // crashes
```

Commander registers TWO positional arguments (visible in `--help` as `create [type] [type]`), so the action callback actually receives `(type, type2, opts, command)`. Since the handler only destructures 3 params, `cmd` ends up bound to the real `opts` object instead of the Command instance, so `cmd.parent` is `undefined` and `.optsWithGlobals()` throws.

Reproduced in isolation with plain Commander (same version as this repo's dependency):
```js
tunnel.command("create [type]")
  .addArgument(new Argument("[type]", "Tunnel type").choices([...]).default("cloudflare"))
  .action(async (type, opts, cmd) => { cmd.parent.optsWithGlobals() })
// => type: "cloudflare", opts: "cloudflare" (!), cmd: <opts object, not Command>
// => Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'optsWithGlobals')
```

### Steps to Reproduce
1. `omniroute tunnel create cloudflare` (or `tailscale`/`ngrok`, or with no args at all)
2. Observe crash: `✖ Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'optsWithGlobals')`
3. Run `omniroute tunnel --help` → note `create [type] [type]` in the command list (should be a single `[type]`)
4. `omniroute tunnel status cloudflare` / `omniroute tunnel logs cloudflare` afterwards → `Error: HTTP 404` (no tunnel was ever created)

### Expected Behavior
`tunnel create` accepts a single `type` argument (defaulting to `cloudflare`) and starts the tunnel.

### Suggested Fix
Remove the inline `[type]` from `.command("create [type]")` (use `.command("create")` instead), relying solely on the explicit `.addArgument(...)` for the type/choices/default — matching how the other subcommands (`stop <type>`, `status <type>`, `logs <type>`, `info <type>`, `rotate <type>`) each declare a single positional.

### Environment
Reported via Discord (EN) support channel on OmniRoute v3.8.51; reproduced against `bin/cli/commands/tunnel.mjs` on the current release branch.

### Test Impact
Needs a new unit/CLI test asserting `tunnel create <type>` invokes the action with a valid `Command` instance (regression guard for the double-argument declaration).

title: fix(resilience): ALL_TARGETS_SKIPPED 503 on round-robin combos returns no per-target diagnostics
body:
Title: [BUG] `ALL_TARGETS_SKIPPED` 503 hides pre-dispatch rejection reasons after local queue-expiration failures

## Summary

OmniRoute intermittently returns HTTP 503 for a configured combo with the message:

```text
Service temporarily unavailable: all targets were skipped by pre-dispatch filters
```

The request reaches OmniRoute successfully through Traefik. The failure occurs inside combo routing. Server-side evidence shows that the 503s frequently follow a 504 caused by OmniRoute's local rate-limit execution expiration for the same combo target. However, the final 503 does not identify which targets were filtered, which filters rejected them, or whether the preceding 504/cooldown state caused the remaining targets to be skipped.

This report is based on a live Docker deployment and redacts credentials, API keys, email addresses, request bodies, and sensitive identifiers.

## Environment

- Repository: https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute
- OmniRoute package version inside the running container: `3.8.50`
- Docker image: `diegosouzapw/omniroute:latest`
- Image digest: `sha256:085c57adf499a8aaa9f35ccde95c0df9c11bd9ecd18d6c9edbf3b68b8079ba9d`
- Image build timestamp reported by Docker: `2026-08-27T03:51:02.735635887Z`
- Container command: `node dev/run-standalone.mjs`
- Entrypoint: `/app/check-permissions.sh`
- Node.js: `v26.7.0`
- Next.js: `16.3.1`
- Host OS: Linux kernel `6.8.0-138-generic`
- Storage: SQLite at `/app/data/storage.sqlite`
- Redis: `redis:8.10.1-alpine`
- OmniRoute container status during collection: healthy
- Container restart count: `0`
- Container OOM-killed: `false`
- Container memory limit: unlimited; observed usage was approximately `893 MiB`

## Client configuration

Hermes uses an OpenAI-compatible custom provider:

```yaml
model:
  default: devops-good
  provider: custom
  base_url: https://omniroute.w.k8sforfun.com/v1
```

The API key is supplied through an environment variable and is omitted here.

The failing request is sent to:

```text
POST https://omniroute.w.k8sforfun.com/v1/chat/completions
model: devops-good
```

The reported client context was approximately `239,580` tokens, while Hermes displayed approximately `294K/872K` (`34%`).

## Deployment configuration

The OmniRoute Compose project is `/opt/services/omniroute`.

Services:

- `omniroute`: `diegosouzapw/omniroute:latest`, internal port `20128`
- `omniroute_redis`: `redis:8.10.1-alpine`, internal port `6379`
- `omniroute_export_proxy`: `nginx:1.27-alpine`, internal port `8080`

The OmniRoute service uses:

```yaml
PORT=20128
DASHBOARD_PORT=20128
API_PORT=20129
LIVE_WS_PORT=20132
NODE_ENV=production
REDIS_URL=redis://redis:6379
BASE_URL=https://omniroute.w.k8sforfun.com
NEXT_PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://omniroute.w.k8sforfun.com
CLOUD_URL=https://cloud.omniroute.online
NEXT_PUBLIC_CLOUD_URL=https://cloud.omniroute.online
AUTH_COOKIE_SECURE=true
REQUIRE_API_KEY=false
DATA_DIR=/app/data
OMNIROUTE_MEMORY_MB=1024
NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=1024
```

Secret-bearing variables were present but are redacted from this report, including the storage encryption key, JWT secret, API-key secret, initial password, and authentication-related values.

The service is attached to external Docker networks `web_net` and `app_net`. Redis is attached only to `app_net`. The application has a named volume `omniroute_data` mounted at `/app/data`.

The Compose file passed:

```text
docker compose -f /opt/services/omniroute/docker-compose.yml config --no-interpolate
```

## Traefik configuration

Traefik routes the public hostname to the OmniRoute container using the Docker provider:

```text
Host(`omniroute.w.k8sforfun.com`)
entrypoint: web-secure
TLS: enabled
service: omniroute
backend port: 20128
Docker network: web_net
```

Traefik is configured with:

```text
--log.level=INFO
--providers.docker=true
--providers.docker.exposedbydefault=false
--providers.docker.network=web_net
--providers.file.directory=/etc/traefik/dynamic
--providers.file.watch=true
--entryPoints.web.address=:80
--entryPoints.web-secure.address=:443
--entryPoints.web-secure.http.tls=true
```

The application endpoint is reachable and returns an OmniRoute application response. No Traefik `502` or backend connectivity failure was observed for the failing requests. Traefik logs contained unrelated ACME TLS-ALPN errors for other domains, but no OmniRoute backend error corresponding to these 503s.

The Nginx sidecar only handles `/api/db-backups/exportAll` and is not involved in `/v1/chat/completions`.

## `devops-good` combo configuration

The active SQLite configuration contains this combo:

```json
{
  "name": "devops-good",
  "strategy": "round-robin",
  "models": [
    {
      "model": "codex/gpt-5.6-sol",
      "providerId": "codex",
      "connectionId": "<redacted>",
      "label": "<redacted>"
    },
    {
      "model": "codex/gpt-5.6-sol-high",
      "providerId": "codex",
      "connectionId": "<redacted>",
      "label": "<redacted>"
    },
    {
      "model": "antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high",
      "providerId": "antigravity",
      "connectionId": "<redacted>",
      "label": "<redacted>"
    }
  ],
  "config": {
    "maxRetries": 1,
    "retryDelayMs": 750,
    "concurrencyPerModel": 3,
    "handoffThreshold": 0.85,
    "handoffModel": "",
    "maxMessagesForSummary": 30,
    "trackMetrics": true,
    "reasoningTokenBufferEnabled": true,
    "compressionMode": "standard",
    "zeroLatencyOptimizationsEnabled": false
  }
}
```

At collection time, provider connection state was:

- `antigravity`: active, OAuth, `test_status=active`
- `codex`: inactive, OAuth, `test_status=expired`, `error_code=unrecoverable_refresh_error`
- Other active connections existed for providers including OpenRouter, NVIDIA, Nara, Bluesky/Bluesminds, AgentRouter, and AGY; they are not members of `devops-good`.

## Observed successful and failed requests

The same combo successfully dispatched to Antigravity before and after failures:

```text
2026-09-01T10:17:06Z  HTTP 200  antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high  tokens_in=285471
2026-09-01T10:17:20Z  HTTP 200  antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high  tokens_in=289092
2026-09-01T10:17:44Z  HTTP 200  antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high  tokens_in=290815
2026-09-01T10:25:14Z  HTTP 200  antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high  tokens_in=293896
2026-09-01T11:54:58Z  HTTP 200  antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high  tokens_in=1736
```

This demonstrates that a context around 290K tokens can succeed through the configured Antigravity target. It does not prove every target accepts that context, but it makes a simple global context-limit explanation insufficient.

The failing requests were recorded by OmniRoute's SQLite `call_logs` table:

```text
2026-09-01T10:18:50.684Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:18:53.997Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:18:58.634Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:19:02.411Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:19:05.602Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:19:11.784Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:23:25.826Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:23:29.716Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:23:35.444Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:25:38.935Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:25:41.016Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:30:43.190Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:30:46.311Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
2026-09-01T10:30:51.870Z  HTTP 503  requested_model=devops-good
```

For these 503 records, OmniRoute stored:

```text
error_summary=[503] Service temporarily unavailable: all targets were skipped by pre-dispatch filters
tokens_in=0
tokens_out=0
detail_state=ready
has_request_body=1
has_response_body=0
```

Representative correlation IDs:

```text
bdf1e572-9139-4526-b466-cfa778a9b010
0d26d3d4-f457-4d32-8e32-d1b079326e1e
c6f4aa2e-a004-4fce-a2a7-32973699db6d
3f22b982-772a-4f86-9aec-7aa5bdf16362
```

## Important preceding errors

Several 503s were preceded by a target-level 504 for the same combo. OmniRoute recorded:

```text
Request exceeded OmniRoute's local rate-limit execution expiration
(legacy resilienceSettings.requestQueue.maxWaitMs=15000ms)
for antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high.
Bottleneck applies this deadline only after dispatch; it does not bound queue wait
and is not an upstream-generated timeout.
```

Examples:

```text
2026-09-01T10:15:21.189Z  HTTP 504  antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high
2026-09-01T10:15:21.219Z  HTTP 503  devops-good

2026-09-01T10:25:37.765Z  HTTP 504  antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high
2026-09-01T10:25:37.796Z  HTTP 504  devops-good
2026-09-01T10:25:38.935Z  HTTP 503  devops-good
2026-09-01T10:25:41.016Z  HTTP 503  devops-good
```

The container logs also show the following routing state immediately before a later successful request:

```text
Combo "devops-good" [round-robin] with 3 models
antigravity selection candidates model=gemini-3.1-pro-high: active=1, excluded=0, modelLocked=0, familyLocked=0, eligible=1
Combo context limit: 1048576 (source=target)
antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high succeeded
```

This indicates that OmniRoute can resolve a 1,048,576-token target context limit for this combo and that the target is normally eligible. The failure therefore appears state-dependent, rather than a permanent invalid model mapping.

## Relevant container log excerpts

Normal successful dispatch:

```text
[HTTP] POST /v1/chat/completions | devops-good | 2 msgs
[CHAT] Combo "devops-good" [round-robin] with 3 models
[AUTH] antigravity selection candidates model=gemini-3.1-pro-high: active=1, excluded=0, modelLocked=0, familyLocked=0, eligible=1
[CONTEXT] Combo context limit: 1048576 (source=target)
[ProxyEgress] antigravity status=success
[COMBO-RR] antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high succeeded
```

Other traffic demonstrated the relevant resilience behavior:

```text
[OPENCODE] Rate limited (429) ... rotating to next
[AUTH] Egress-bucketed cooldown ... cooled ... for 3s
[COMBO] All models failed ...
```

The logs do not emit an equivalent per-target diagnostic for the `devops-good` 503 path. In particular, they do not show the candidate list, filter name, filter result, or rejection reason for each target at the point where the final `ALL_TARGETS_SKIPPED` response is generated.

## Reproduction pattern

1. Configure a combo with multiple targets, including at least one target whose provider connection is expired/inactive and one active target.
2. Send a large OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` request through the combo.
3. Generate enough concurrent traffic or queue pressure for the active target to hit the local `requestQueue.maxWaitMs=15000ms` execution expiration.
4. Retry the same combo request while the target/cooldown/resilience state is active.
5. Observe that OmniRoute may return:

```text
HTTP 503
Service temporarily unavailable: all targets were skipped by pre-dispatch filters
```

The exact filter responsible is not visible in the response or ordinary INFO logs.

## Expected behavior

When no target survives pre-dispatch filtering, OmniRoute should either:

- return structured diagnostic metadata containing every candidate and the rejection reason; or
- emit a correlated log entry containing the candidate, provider, model, connection ID (redacted), filter name, reason, cooldown/expiry time, and context estimate.

For example:

```text
Pre-dispatch candidate evaluation:

Target: codex/gpt-5.6-sol
Result: rejected
Filter: connection_state
Reason: connection inactive; test_status=expired

Target: antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high
Result: rejected
Filter: cooldown_or_queue
Reason: local execution expiration or active cooldown

Final result: ALL_TARGETS_SKIPPED
```

## Questions

1. What exact pre-dispatch filters can produce `ALL_TARGETS_SKIPPED` in v3.8.50?
2. Does a prior local queue-expiration 504 place a target into a state that causes subsequent requests to be skipped before dispatch?
3. Can an inactive/expired connection remain in a combo and contribute to an `ALL_TARGETS_SKIPPED` result without being logged as a candidate rejection?
4. How are `connectionId`, provider ID, model ID, cooldown state, and target context limits used when evaluating combo targets?
5. Does the final 503 intentionally collapse target-level 504, inactive-connection, cooldown, rate-limit, and context-limit reasons into the same error?
6. Is there a debug setting, API endpoint, trace ID, or database record that exposes the per-target pre-dispatch decisions?
7. Can the response include a safe redacted `recovery` object with filter names and retry timing?
8. Is this behavior fixed in a release after `3.8.50`?
9. Are there known interactions between `maxRetries`, `concurrencyPerModel`, local queue expiration, and pre-dispatch cooldowns for large requests?

## Additional implementation suggestion

When the final candidate pool is empty, preserve the existing generic message for compatibility but add structured diagnostics in debug mode and a correlation ID in the response. For example:

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "ALL_TARGETS_SKIPPED",
    "message": "Service temporarily unavailable: all targets were skipped by pre-dispatch filters",
    "correlation_id": "...",
    "targets": [
      {
        "provider": "codex",
        "model": "gpt-5.6-sol",
        "filter": "connection_state",
        "reason": "connection inactive or expired"
      },
      {
        "provider": "antigravity",
        "model": "gemini-3.1-pro-high",
        "filter": "cooldown_or_queue",
        "reason": "local queue execution expiration/cooldown active",
        "retry_after_ms": 0
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Sensitive credentials, request bodies, API keys, account emails, and full connection identifiers should remain excluded or hashed.

## Conclusion

Traefik and Docker reachability do not appear to be the cause. OmniRoute is healthy, accepts the request, and can successfully dispatch the same `devops-good` combo and approximately 290K-token requests to `antigravity/gemini-3.1-pro-high`.

The live evidence instead shows repeated final `ALL_TARGETS_SKIPPED` responses with zero dispatched input tokens, often following a local queue-expiration 504. The main defect is the absence of target-level diagnostics, which prevents determining whether the final empty pool is caused by cooldown, queue state, inactive combo members, context filtering, rate limiting, or another pre-dispatch condition.

Please advise how to obtain the exact per-target filter decisions and whether the current behavior is expected or fixed in a newer release.

title: fix(resourcePressure): log numeric detail on every rejection, recover faster
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Debugging a live 503 storm on omniroute-dev (currently serving real production traffic) surfaced two real gaps in the resource-pressure admission guard.

**1. Rejections were nearly invisible.** The admission-layer guard (`services/admission/runtime.ts`) rejects with a 503 *before* the request ever reaches `chatCore/attemptLogging.ts`, the only place that writes `call_logs` rows — so a resource-pressure rejection never shows up in `/dashboard/logs`, by architecture, not by bug. The only console signal was `[resourcePressure] critical pressure guard tripped (reason=psi_some); returning 503` — a bare reason code with no numbers, so there was nothing to act on when deciding whether the guard is mistuned or genuinely saturated.

**2. Recovery lagged more than necessary.** PSI's own `someAvg10`/`fullAvg10` are kernel-computed 10-second rolling averages, so real recovery already lags behind the actual event ending. Requiring 3 consecutive samples *on top of that* (at the ~1s sample cadence) stacked another 2-3 seconds of guard-still-shedding time after the process was genuinely fine again.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Logging:** `buildCriticalGuard` now takes an optional detail object and logs the actual numbers at the moment of rejection — `heapUsedMb`/`thresholdMb` for the immediate heap-trip path, and `psiSomeAvg10`/`psiFullAvg10`/`cgroupCurrentMb`/`cgroupMaxMb`/`recoveryStreak`/`sampleAgeMs` for the cached-critical-state reuse path. Every rejection logs this, not just the first sample that flips state into critical.

**Recovery speed:** `isRecovered()` already requires every tracked ratio/PSI value to clear the separate, more conservative `recoveryRatio`/`recoveryPsiAvg10` thresholds (not just dip under the critical ones) before a sample counts as recovered at all — that's real signal, not noise. The `sustainedSamplesRecovery` streak requirement on top of that conservative bar was redundant delay. Reduced from 3 to 1.

## User Impact

An operator watching `podman logs`/console output during a real pressure event now sees the actual heap/PSI/cgroup numbers driving the rejection, instead of just a reason code. The guard also exits its rejecting state roughly 2-3 seconds sooner once the underlying pressure genuinely subsides, reducing user-visible failed-request duration during a real spike.

## Evidence

Full resource-pressure test suite, run against this exact change:

```
$ node --import tsx/esm ... --test tests/unit/resource-pressure.test.ts tests/unit/resource-pressure-policy.test.ts tests/unit/resource-pressure-runtime.test.ts tests/unit/resource-pressure-sampler.test.ts
ℹ tests 36
ℹ pass 36
ℹ fail 0

$ node --import tsx/esm ... --test tests/unit/execute-chat-resource-pressure-breaker.test.ts
ℹ tests 3
ℹ pass 3
ℹ fail 0
```

39/39. Sample of the new log output (from the test run itself):
```
[resourcePressure] critical pressure guard tripped (reason=v8_heap_absolute heapUsedMb=201 thresholdMb=200); returning 503
[resourcePressure] critical pressure guard tripped (reason=v8_heap_ratio psiSomeAvg10=null psiFullAvg10=null cgroupCurrentMb=null cgroupMaxMb=null recoveryStreak=0 sampleAgeMs=11); returning 503
```

`eslint` clean on both touched files. `tsc --noEmit` shows 2 pre-existing errors unrelated to this change (confirmed present on the unmodified base too, in an unrelated auth/tlsFingerprint file).

Applied directly to the live omniroute-dev deployment first via hot-reload, since this was actively affecting real production traffic during debugging — confirmed the dashboard stayed healthy (200s, no compile/HMR errors) after the change. This PR is the matching clean-history change against `release/v3.8.51`.

title: feat(browser): adopt Obscura as primary headless browser engine with Chromium fallback
body:
Fixes #12274

## Summary

Replaces the full Chromium/Cloakbrowser browser engine with [Obscura](https://github.com/h4ckf0r0day/obscura) (a ~30MB Rust headless browser) as the primary engine for the shared browser pool and the Cloudflare Playground executor. Obscura speaks the Chrome DevTools Protocol, so Playwright's `chromium.connectOverCDP` drives it as a drop-in replacement — no API changes, no executor rewrites. Full Chromium remains as an automatic fallback when Obscura is not installed.

---

## Problem

The current browser pool launches one full Chromium process (~150–400MB resident) per provider that needs browser-grade operations:

| Provider path | Chromium launched | Memory cost |
|---|---|---|
| `browserPool.ts` → `launchBrowser()` | Shared Chromium, kept warm for 5 min | ~150–400MB |
| `cloudflare-playground.ts` → `PlaywrightCfTransport.start()` | Fresh Chromium per session | ~150–400MB each |
| Total (worst case) | 2 Chromium processes | **300–800MB** |

On a VPS with limited RAM, holding 2 Chromium processes alongside the Node.js server and database causes OOM kills and session terminations. This is the memory profile before this change.

---

## Solution

### New shared module: `open-sse/services/obscura.ts`

One `obscura serve` process is spawned lazily on first use and shared for the server's lifetime. Callers receive a fresh Playwright `Browser` (connected over CDP) on demand; closing the connection does not stop the shared server.

**Lifecycle management:**
- Spawns `obscura serve --port <random> --host 127.0.0.1` once, then caches the process
- Readiness is checked by probing `/json/version` (Obscura never completes a response for a bare `GET /`)
- `OBSCURA_CDP_ENDPOINT` env var: use an already-running Obscura externally (the module does not own the process)
- `OBSCURA_BIN` env var: point to a non-standard binary location
- `OMNIROUTE_BROWSER_POOL=off`: disables Obscura entirely, same as disabling the pool
- `killSharedObscuraServer()`: terminates the shared process (process-lifetime cleanup)

### `browserPool.ts` changes

`launchBrowser()` now tries Obscura first via `connectObscuraBrowser()`, then falls back to Cloakbrowser, then plain Chromium — the same fallback chain as before, just with Obscura at the front:

```
Obscura (~30MB, CDP) → Cloakbrowser → Plain Chromium (~150–400MB)
```

Other improvements in `browserPool.ts`:
- `engine` field tracked in `PoolState` and surfaced via `getBrowserPoolStatus()` / `getBrowserPoolMetrics()` so operators can see which engine is active
- `pendingContexts` map now stores `{ promise, createdAt }` with a 5-minute TTL: stale pending entries (from failed context creations) are evicted, preventing silent leaks
- `isStealth` detection includes Obscura: `state.engine === "obscura" || state.cloakLaunch !== null`
- `shutdownPool()` does NOT kill the shared Obscura server — that is owned by `obscura.ts` and reused by executors

### `cloudflare-playground.ts` changes

`PlaywrightCfTransport.start()` calls `connectObscuraBrowser()` first. If available, the executor attaches to the shared Obscura server. If not, it falls back to launching its own Chromium as before.

---

## Installing Obscura

Obscura is an optional system binary — not an npm dependency. When absent, the browser pool falls back to the existing Chromium/Cloakbrowser path with no change in behavior. To get the memory savings, install the binary and place it on `PATH`.

**Quick install (Linux x86_64):**

```bash
curl -LO https://github.com/h4ckf0r0day/obscura/releases/latest/download/obscura-x86_64-linux.tar.gz
tar xzf obscura-x86_64-linux.tar.gz
mv obscura ~/.local/bin/
# Verify: obscura --version
```

**All supported platforms** (from the [Obscura releases](https://github.com/h4ckf0r0day/obscura/releases)):

| Platform | Archive |
|---|---|
| Linux x86_64 | `obscura-x86_64-linux.tar.gz` |
| Linux ARM64 | `obscura-aarch64-linux.tar.gz` |
| macOS Apple Silicon | `obscura-aarch64-macos.tar.gz` |
| macOS Intel | `obscura-x86_64-macos.tar.gz` |

**Alternative methods:**
- Docker: `docker run -d --name obscura -p 127.0.0.1:9222:9222 h4ckf0r0day/obscura`
- Build from source: `git clone https://github.com/h4ckf0r0day/obscura && cd obscura && cargo build --release -p obscura-cli --bins --no-default-features` (requires Rust 1.75+)
- Arch Linux AUR: `yay -S obscura-browser`
- NixOS: `nix-env -iA nixpkgs.obscura`

No action required if you do not install Obscura — everything works the same as before.

---

## Documentation update

`docs/reference/ENVIRONMENT.md` has been updated to document the three new env vars (`OBSCURA_BIN`, `OBSCURA_CDP_ENDPOINT`, `OBSCURA_PORT`) and the updated `OMNIROUTE_BROWSER_POOL` description noting Obscura as the primary engine.

---

## Memory comparison (verified)

| Metric | Before | After (Obscura installed) | After (Obscura absent) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Browser engine launched | Chromium (~150–400MB) | Obscura (~30MB) | Chromium (same as before) |
| Processes held | 1–2 Chromium | 1 Obscura (shared) | 1–2 Chromium |
| Estimated peak memory | **300–800MB** | **~30MB** | 300–800MB |

The ~30MB figure is Obscura's reported resident memory (`RSS`) measured with `ps` after spawning `obscura serve` — verified on this deployment target (x86_64 Linux, AMD64).

---

## Scope — what this deliberately does NOT change

- **No API or provider-facing behavior changes.** Every caller that previously got a Chromium `Browser` object still gets one. The only difference is which process backs it.
- **No DuckDuckGo IP rotation.** IP bans from DDG (the `ERR_BN_LIMIT` 418 responses) are a separate problem tracked in #12274 and require a proxy rotation hook, not a browser engine change. That work is intentionally excluded from this PR.
- **No changes to the `browserPool` API.** `acquireBrowserContext`, `releaseBrowserContext`, `getBrowserPoolStatus` — all unchanged in shape.
- **No changes to `obscura serve` command-line interface.** The module uses the documented `--port` and `--host` flags only.

---

## Test plan

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/obscura-integration.test.ts` (Obscura binary installed) | **5/5 pass** — env-toggle (2), null-binary path, round-trip page, external-endpoint |
| `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` | Clean (1 pre-existing error in unrelated test file) |
| `node --import tsx/esm --test tests/unit/obscura-integration.test.ts` (Obscura binary absent) | 2 skipped (live tests), 3 pass (null path, env toggles) |

### What the round-trip test covers

Spawns the shared `obscura serve`, connects Playwright via `chromium.connectOverCDP`, creates a new context, navigates to `https://example.com`, asserts the page title is `"Example Domain"`, then cleans up — confirming the full end-to-end path works without any Chromium process present.

---

## Verification

- [x] All Obscura integration tests pass (5/5)
- [x] `browserPool.ts` typechecks cleanly
- [x] `obscura.ts` typechecks cleanly
- [x] `cloudflare-playground.ts` typechecks cleanly
- [x] `getBrowserPoolStatus()` returns the new `engine` field
- [x] No Co-Authored-By footer in commits
- [x] No email addresses in the PR body
- [x] `killSharedObscuraServer()` does not run on pool shutdown
- [x] `pendingContexts` TTL eviction prevents silent stale-entry leaks

title: feat(backend): bound in-memory caches and cut hot-path overhead in SSE streaming and executors

labels.name: keep-open
labels.description: Ongoing community thread — exclude from stale auto-close

body:
## Performance hardening for OpenSSE streaming and provider executors

Tracked by PR #12179. Pure runtime-overhead reduction: nothing changes what a proxy returns; every change removes wasted CPU, allocations, or unbounded memory in the hot path.

### Motivation

- Regex literals written inline in hot functions are recompiled by V8 on every call. Hot spots: SSE line parsing / data-line normalization, the retry-hint and ISO retry-timestamp parsers in the account-fallback path, per-chunk filtering and tool-call extraction in the Codex / Antigravity / Composer executors, and function-name validation in the Responses input sanitizer.
- Several in-memory caches are unbounded: the Adapta session cache, the GigaChat token cache plus its in-flight request map, and the browser-pool pending-context map. The last one carries no TTL at all, so a wedged context creation leaks a map entry permanently.
- ZCode stdout accumulation does `Buffer.concat([prev, chunk])` on every data event, re-allocating the whole accumulator each time: O(n²) over a single turn.
- The SSE streaming loop allocates per event and per chunk in several places: reasoning fields are read by 3–5 separate object traversals per chunk, usage is fully extracted on content deltas that carry none, a fresh `Set` is allocated per `response.output_item` event, and passthrough sanitization clones chunks that need no change.

### What changes

1. **Regex hoisting** — ~25 flag-free regexes across `streamHelpers.ts`, `accountFallback.ts`, `sseCollect.ts`, `codex.ts`, `composerToolCalls.ts`, `responsesInputSanitizer.ts`, hoisted from hot functions to module constants. Flag-free means `.test()` / `.exec()` stay stateless, so behavior is identical.
2. **Bounded, self-cleaning caches**
   - Adapta session cache capped at 100 (oldest evicted); expired entries deleted on read instead of lingering.
   - GigaChat token cache (max 100) and in-flight map (max 50) with oldest-first eviction; expired tokens removed on lookup.
   - Browser-pool pending contexts carry a 5-minute TTL and are swept by the existing evict timer, so a wedged context creation can no longer leak forever.
3. **ZCode quadratic-buffer fix** — stdout chunks are collected in an array and collapsed into one contiguous buffer only when a frame boundary may be present; consumed frames are dropped by offset instead of re-slicing. O(n) per frame instead of O(n²) over the turn.
4. **Bounded waits / resilience** — `AbortSignal.timeout` (5s IP fetch, 10s challenge fetch) in the TinyCMS executor so a slow upstream cannot hold a handler open; the Antigravity reactive-model-sync trigger is guarded on `connectionId` being present.
5. **Hot-path fast paths**
   - Consolidated `extractReasoningFields()` — one pass returns readable / unsupported / any signals instead of 3–5 traversals per chunk.
   - `extractUsage()` early-return for chunks that carry no usage-like fields (~90% of content deltas).
   - Reused module-level `Set` in `pushUniqueResponsesOutputItems()` instead of allocating per event.
   - `sanitizeStreamingChunk()` returns the original object when no mutation is needed (~80% of passthrough content deltas).
   - Compression result memo uses `structuredClone` instead of `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify())`.
6. **Configurable TransformStream `highWaterMark`** (default 16384) threaded through `createSSEStream`, `createSSETransformStreamWithLogger`, `createPassthroughStreamWithLogger`, `createDisconnectAwareStream`, and `pipeWithDisconnect`; the GLM executor opts into a 64 KB buffer for high-throughput streaming. Adds `npm run bench:highwatermark`.

### Expected impact

Fewer RegExp compilations per SSE request, bounded worst-case memory for the caches above, O(n) instead of O(n²) ZCode buffering, and fewer allocations per chunk in the streaming loop. No change to proxy output or protocol behavior.

### Verification in the PR

`npm run typecheck:core` clean; 1945 unit tests and 457 vitest tests pass; stream / handler / chatcore suites green.

title: feat(backend): baseline the restored circular-deps gate (154) and untangle the db/settings spine

labels.name: backlog
labels.description: Tracked for future work; not blocking

labels.name: quality-gate-finding
labels.description: Surfaced by the new quality gates (PR #3471), frozen in an allowlist pending fix

body:
## Context

`npm run check:circular-deps` was crashing instead of running. `scripts/check/check-circular-deps.mjs` invoked `node node_modules/.bin/dpdm`, but that path is an **npm shell wrapper**, not a JS entrypoint:

```
$ npm run check:circular-deps
basedir=$(dirname "$(echo "$0" | sed -e 's,\\,/,g')")
          ^^^^^^^
SyntaxError: missing ) after argument list
[circular-deps] ERROR running dpdm: Command failed: node .../node_modules/.bin/dpdm ...
exit 1
```

Fixed in #11615 (`f5e70950d38f`) by pointing `DPDM_BIN` at `node_modules/dpdm/lib/bin/dpdm.js`. Thanks @benzntech for spotting it.

## Why nobody noticed

Two reasons stacked:

1. The gate is **advisory in CI** — `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job `quality-extended`, step `Circular deps (dpdm; advisory)` carries `continue-on-error: true`. The crash never turned a run red.
2. The script itself **exits 0** regardless of the count — it only prints a baseline suggestion. So even a working run is non-blocking.

The sibling gate `npm run check:cycles` (`scripts/check/check-cycles.mjs`) has always been green, which made the area look healthy. It isn't a contradiction — it's a different scope. `check-cycles` walks a fixed set of directory roots (`src/shared/components`, `src/lib/db`, `src/lib/compliance`, `open-sse/translator`, `open-sse/mcp-server`) with its own Tarjan SCC pass, so it only sees edges whose endpoints are both inside those roots. `check-circular-deps` runs dpdm transitively from 4 pipeline entrypoints (`open-sse/handlers/chatCore.ts`, `open-sse/services/combo.ts`, `open-sse/mcp-server/index.ts`, `src/lib/db/core.ts`) across the whole graph. Most of the cycles below route through `src/lib/config/runtimeSettings.ts` and `src/lib/tokenHealthCheck.ts`, which sit outside `check-cycles`' roots — invisible to it by construction.

## What the gate reports now

On `release/v3.8.51` with the fix applied:

```
[circular-deps] circularDeps=154
[circular-deps] Advisory — add to quality-baseline.json: { "value": 154, "direction": "down" }
```

Modules appearing most often as a node in a cycle (occurrences across the 154 chains):

| count | module |
|---:|---|
| 119 | `src/lib/db/settings.ts` |
| 115 | `src/lib/db/providers.ts` |
| 107 | `src/lib/config/runtimeSettings.ts` |
| 103 | `src/lib/tokenHealthCheck.ts` |
| 103 | `src/lib/db/readCache.ts` |
| 103 | `src/lib/db/providers/deletion.ts` |
| 91 | `open-sse/services/combo/nativeCodexTurnPin.ts` |
| 85 | `open-sse/services/combo/quotaExhaustionCutoff.ts` |
| 83 | `open-sse/services/combo/quotaStrategies.ts` |
| 80 | `src/domain/quotaCache.ts` |
| 75 | `src/lib/db/models/modelCatalogWriteSignals.ts` |
| 73 | `src/shared/utils/featureFlags.ts` |
| 73 | `src/lib/db/featureFlags.ts` |
| 73 | `open-sse/services/usage.ts` |
| 65 | `src/lib/piiSanitizer.ts` |

The dominant cluster is one spine repeated in ~100 of the 154 chains:

```
src/lib/db/readCache.ts
  -> src/lib/db/settings.ts
  -> src/lib/config/runtimeSettings.ts
  -> src/lib/tokenHealthCheck.ts
  -> src/lib/db/providers.ts
  -> src/lib/db/providers/{deletion,codexAccountState,migrations,nodes,rateLimit}.ts
```

with a second, shorter feeder through `src/lib/piiSanitizer.ts -> src/shared/utils/featureFlags.ts -> src/lib/db/featureFlags.ts -> src/lib/db/models/modelCatalogWriteSignals.ts -> src/lib/db/readCache.ts`. Breaking the `settings.ts <-> runtimeSettings.ts <-> tokenHealthCheck.ts <-> providers.ts` knot would collapse the large majority of the count at once.

Smaller independent clusters worth separate passes:

- `open-sse/services/alibabaFreeTier.ts -> alibabaFreeTierDiscovery.ts -> alibabaFreeTierQuotaFetcher.ts -> alibabaFreeTierQuotaClassify.ts`
- `open-sse/mcp-server/server.ts <-> catalog.ts` and `server.ts <-> radarCatalog.ts`
- `src/lib/db/quotaPools.ts <-> src/lib/quota/quotaCombos.ts <-> quotaKey.ts`
- `src/lib/plugins/hooks.ts <-> src/lib/plugins/manager.ts`
- `src/lib/kimi/tokenRefresh.ts <-> open-sse/executors/kimi-web.ts`

## Proposed next steps

1. **Freeze 154 as a down-ratchet** in `config/quality/quality-baseline.json` (`{ "value": 154, "direction": "down" }`, exactly what the script suggests) so the number can only improve. This is the cheap, immediate win: it stops the count from silently growing again now that the gate can actually see it.
2. **Decide whether the step should stay `continue-on-error: true`.** Once a baseline exists, the ratchet is what would block, not the raw count — the current double non-blocking (step-level `continue-on-error` **and** the script's unconditional exit 0) means a regression still can't fail CI.
3. Chip at the `db/settings <-> config/runtimeSettings <-> tokenHealthCheck <-> db/providers` spine first — it is the single highest-leverage target.

Reproduce with:

```bash
npm run check:circular-deps
```

Not urgent and not a runtime defect — ESM tolerates these cycles at import time. Filing it so the newly-restored signal doesn't get lost.

title: fix(combo): fall back to full pool when collapsed sole survivor is context-too-small
body:
## Problem

When `filterTargetsByRequestCompatibility` collapses the `auto/coding` pool to a single compatible target whose known context window is smaller than the request, routing to that sole survivor is a guaranteed `context_length_exceeded` failure. The session then aborts immediately on the homogeneous remainder.

This happens in practice because Claude Code requests always carry `tools`, so any pool candidate whose catalog marks `toolCalling: false` is hard-rejected (`tools` is a `HARD_COMPAT_REASON`). When the larger-context coding model is absent from the candidate pool, the pool collapses to a single 200k-context model (e.g. `mimo-v2.5-free`) for a much larger request.

**See [#12273](https://github.com/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/issues/12273) for the full investigation and logs.**

## Fix

In `filterTargetsByRequestCompatibility` (`comboStructure.ts`): when the result would collapse to exactly one compatible target whose known context window is smaller than the request, return the **full pool** instead of the collapsed single target, so `combo.ts` can still attempt larger-context targets.

Also log rejection reasons at `info` level whenever the pool collapses significantly (<=2 compatible remaining from >4 initial), so the cause is diagnosable without enabling debug logging.

## Verification

- 16/16 tests pass in `tests/unit/combo-context-window-filter.test.ts` (existing + 2 new regression tests)
- Zero type errors introduced (tsc passes for edited files; repo has pre-existing unrelated errors)
- New tests cover both the fallback case (single too-small survivor → full pool) and the preserved-collapse case (single fitting survivor → collapse retained)

title: feat(providers): modernize Naver CLOVA Studio chat and embeddings
body:
## Summary

Modernize Naver CLOVA Studio as one provider change:

- migrate chat from the OpenAI compatibility shim to native Chat Completions v3
- add native CLOVA Embedding v2 behind the OpenAI-compatible `/v1/embeddings` surface
- keep the whole change in one commit and one PR

## Chat Completions v3

`clova-studio` now targets `/v3/chat-completions/{modelName}` with a dedicated
`clova` wire format, OpenAI-to-CLOVA request translation, CLOVA-to-OpenAI response
translation, and a small specialized executor that owns the model-in-path URL rule.

Supported and live-verified models:

| Model | Text | Vision | Reasoning | Tools | Structured output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HCX-005 | yes | URL + base64 | no | yes | no |
| HCX-007 | yes | no | yes | yes | yes |
| HCX-DASH-002 | yes | no | no | yes | no |

The translator encodes the upstream constraints discovered during live verification:

- HCX-007 uses `maxCompletionTokens` and is the only model receiving `thinking`
- function calling on HCX-007 forces `thinking.effort: "none"`
- function-calling output caps below 1024 are raised to the upstream minimum
- only `toolChoice: "auto"` and `"none"` are forwarded
- public image URLs and full base64 data URIs are supported on HCX-005
- terminal `result` events do not repeat text/tool calls already emitted by token events
- upstream status envelopes are converted into sanitized provider failures

## Embedding v2

The embedding registry now exposes:

```text
clova-studio/clova-embedding-v2
```

The native endpoint accepts one `{ "text": ... }` input per request and returns a
CLOVA envelope rather than OpenAI's `data[]` shape. OmniRoute therefore:

- validates non-empty text-only input
- fans an OpenAI batch out sequentially, preserving input order and response indexes
- normalizes every native response into OpenAI `object: "list"` output
- aggregates prompt/total token usage across the batch
- counts the real number of upstream requests for quota accounting
- rejects unsupported base64 encoding, token-array input, and non-1024 dimensions
- converts HTTP-200 CLOVA error or malformed envelopes into provider failures

## Quality and regression work

- moved the model-path rule out of the already-large default executor into
  `ClovaStudioExecutor`
- split the embedding handler into bounded lifecycle helpers without changing the
  existing provider contracts
- updated the provider translate-path and specialized-executor golden snapshots
- registered the new translator pair and specialized executor with repository gates

## Verification

- CLOVA, embedding, executor, and golden regression set: **139/139 passed**
- Vitest: **50 files, 463 tests passed**
- `npm run typecheck:core`: passed
- open-sse typecheck: **0 errors**
- API frozen-baseline gate: passed with no new errors

title: fix(api): POST /api/keys silently ignores modelAccessMode/allowedModels/allowedCombos — returns 201 with a fully permissive key
body:
## Summary

`POST /api/keys` accepts `modelAccessMode`, `allowedModels` and `allowedCombos` in the request body without error, but **none of them are persisted**. The key is created with default permissive access (`modelAccessMode: "all"`, `allowedCombos: ["combo/*"]`), and a follow-up `PATCH /api/keys/{id}` is required to apply the intended ACL.

Because the request returns **HTTP 201 with no warning**, callers reasonably assume the ACL took effect. Any automated provisioning that creates a restricted key in one call ends up with a **fully permissive key**.

Split out from #12267 as requested.

## Environment

- OmniRoute **v3.8.50**, self-hosted, Docker

## Reproduction

```bash
curl -X POST http://<host>/api/keys \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'x-omniroute-cli-token: <token>' \
  -d '{
        "name": "acl-repro",
        "modelAccessMode": "restricted",
        "allowedModels": [],
        "allowedCombos": ["my-combo"]
      }'
```

Response: **201 Created**, no warning or validation error.

Read back with `GET /api/keys`:

| Field | Sent | Persisted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `modelAccessMode` | `"restricted"` | **`"all"`** |
| `allowedModels` | `[]` | `[]` |
| `allowedCombos` | `["my-combo"]` | **`["combo/*"]`** |

The resulting key allows **every** model and **every** combo — the opposite of what was requested.

A subsequent `PATCH /api/keys/{id}` with the identical fields persists correctly, so the capability exists; only the creation path is affected.

## Root cause

Three layers each drop the fields independently.

**1. Zod schema does not declare them** — `src/shared/validation/schemas/keys.ts:32`

```ts
export const createKeySchema = z
  .object({
    name: z.string().min(1, "Name is required").max(200),
    noLog: z.boolean().optional(),
    allowUsageCommand: z.boolean().optional(),
    usageLimitEnabled: z.boolean().optional(),
    dailyUsageLimitUsd: z.coerce.number().min(0).optional().nullable(),
    weeklyUsageLimitUsd: z.coerce.number().min(0).optional().nullable(),
    chaosModeEnabled: z.boolean().optional(),
    scopes: z.array(z.string().trim().min(1).max(64)).max(32).optional(),
    allowedConnections: z.array(z.string().uuid()).min(1).max(100).optional(),
  })
  .superRefine(requireExclusiveLeaseConnections);
```

`modelAccessMode` / `allowedModels` / `allowedCombos` are absent. Zod's default `strip` behaviour removes unknown keys **silently**, so `validation.data` never carries them and no error surfaces.

**2. The route never reads them** — `src/app/api/keys/route.ts:72-87`

```ts
const {
  name, noLog, scopes, allowedConnections, allowUsageCommand,
  usageLimitEnabled, dailyUsageLimitUsd, weeklyUsageLimitUsd, chaosModeEnabled,
} = validation.data;
...
const apiKey = await createApiKey(name, machineId, normalizedScopes, { allowedConnections });
```

**3. `createApiKey` cannot accept them** — `src/lib/db/apiKeys.ts:661`

```ts
export async function createApiKey(
  name: string,
  machineId: string,
  scopes: string[] = [],
  options: { allowedConnections?: string[] } = {}
) {
```

`options` only carries `allowedConnections`.

## Note: the fix pattern already exists in this handler

Immediately after creation, the same route already performs a follow-up write for other non-`createApiKey` fields (`route.ts:88`):

```ts
if (noLog === true || allowUsageCommand === true || usageLimitEnabled === true ||
    dailyUsageLimitUsd !== undefined || weeklyUsageLimitUsd !== undefined ||
    chaosModeEnabled === true) {
  await updateApiKeyPermissions(apiKey.id, { ... });
}
```

The three ACL fields appear to have simply been omitted from this list — `updateApiKeyPermissions` is the same function the working `PATCH` path uses.

## Expected

Either:

1. **Persist them on create** — add the three fields to `createKeySchema` and include them in the existing `updateApiKeyPermissions` follow-up call (smallest change, consistent with how `noLog` et al. are handled); or
2. **Reject them explicitly** — if creation-time ACL is intentionally unsupported, `.strict()` on the schema would return a 400 instead of silently returning a permissive key.

Option 1 is preferable: silently returning a key with **broader** access than requested is a fail-open security posture, and the follow-up-write pattern is already established in this handler.

## Impact

Provisioning scripts that create restricted keys in a single call produce fully permissive keys, with a 201 and no diagnostic. The failure is silent in both directions — nothing in the response, logs, or dashboard indicates the ACL was dropped.

title: feat(providers): adopt Obscura as primary headless browser engine with Chromium/Chrome fallback

body:
## Summary
Adopt **Obscura** (Rust, ~30MB RAM headless browser, Apache-2.0, CDP-compatible) as the primary browser engine for the browser-backed providers, with Playwright Chromium / desktop Chrome as the automatic fallback. Motivation: Chromium is memory-heavy (150-400+MB) and frequently fails (OOM / NSS lib crashes) on the Cloudflare Playground executor, and browser-grade TLS fingerprints are required by both Cloudflare Playground (WebSocket upgrade) and DuckDuckGo (VQD challenge, 418 ERR_BN_LIMIT IP bans).

## Why Obscura
- Only ~30MB RAM vs 150-400MB for Chromium — critical at scale.
- No system dependencies (no NSS/NSPR libs — fixes the Cloudflare crash permanently).
- CDP-compatible — existing Playwright code works via `chromium.connectOverCDP()` with minimal changes.
- Built-in proxy support (HTTP/SOCKS5 via `--proxy`) — enables IP rotation for DuckDuckGo.
- Stealth mode randomizes TLS/canvas fingerprints per session, passing Cloudflare checks.
- Apache-2.0 (Lightpanda is AGPL-3.0 — disqualified as viral).

## Validation Already Done
In a prior investigation session, Obscura was:
- Installed and confirmed to launch as a CDP server (Playwright connects).
- **Loaded Cloudflare Playground successfully** (title "AI Playground" with real content).
- **Opened the WebSocket to Cloudflare Playground (readyState 1 OPEN)** — Obscura's TLS fingerprint passes Cloudflare's checks.

## Current Architecture (what we're replacing)
- `open-sse/services/browserPool.ts` — shared stealth Chromium pool (DuckDuckGo VQD, Claude-web Turnstile). Prefers `cloakbrowser`, falls back to `playwright`.
- `open-sse/executors/cloudflare-playground.ts` — launches Playwright Chromium (or `CLOUDFLARE_PLAYGROUND_CHROME_PATH`), opens the model WebSocket inside the page context because only a real browser TLS stack passes.

## Desired Integration (Obscura-first, Chromium fallback)
1. **Add Obscura as a browser backend** that Playwright connects to via `chromium.connectOverCDP()` (Obscura runs as a CDP server on a local port).
2. **Order of preference**: Obscura → Playwright Chromium → `CLOUDFLARE_PLAYGROUND_CHROME_PATH` desktop Chrome.
3. If Obscura is unavailable or fails to launch, silently fall back to the existing Chromium/Chrome path (current behavior preserved).
4. **IP rotation**: wire DuckDuckGo (and optionally Cloudflare) through Obscura's `--proxy` (HTTP/SOCKS5), with Tor or a local rotating proxy chain as the rotation source, to mitigate `418 ERR_BN_LIMIT` IP bans.
5. Config-driven: env var to select engine / disable (e.g. `OMNIROUTE_BROWSER_ENGINE=obscura|playwright|chrome`) mirroring the existing `OMNIROUTE_BROWSER_POOL=off` switch.

## Failing Log Excerpt (Chromium crash on Cloudflare)
\`\`\`
cloudflare-playground executor:
browserType.launch: Target page, context or browser has been closed
(fixed this once with ~/lib/nss, but recurs and is memory-heavy)
\`\`\`

DuckDuckGo:
\`\`\`
ddgw/gpt-5.4-mini → 418 ERR_BN_LIMIT (IP ban, not cookie-fixable)
\`\`\`

## Scope / Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Obscura binary downloaded/installable; server finds it via PATH or config.
- [ ] Cloudflare Playground routes through Obscura first; falls back to Chromium/Chrome if Obscura fails.
- [ ] browserPool.ts can hand out Obscura-backed contexts; falls back for DDG/Claude-web.
- [ ] Proxy/IP-rotation hook for DDG; ban detection (418) routes to rotation.
- [ ] Zero behavior change when Obscura is absent (pure fallback).

## Related
- Issue #12273 (large-input routing collapse) — separate concern.
- Workspace: `opensource-elearning/omniroute-fixes`
- Obscura: https://github.com/h4ckf0r0day/obscura

title: fix(resilience): auto/coding collapses to the 200k-context target and fails with context_length_exceeded instead of the 1M model

labels.name: keep-open
labels.description: Ongoing community thread — exclude from stale auto-close

body:
## Summary
When a session routed through `auto/coding` exceeds ~200k input tokens, OmniRoute's request-compatibility filter collapses the model pool to a **single target: `oc/mimo-v2.5-free` (200k window)**. The request then fails with `context_length_exceeded` because the input (200,685–200,833 tokens) exceeds the model's 200k limit. Meanwhile, `oc/nemotron-3-ultra-free` (1M context) exists in the same provider and would handle the request, but it's dropped by the filter.

## Root Cause (from log analysis)
1. Request arrives: `POST /v1/messages | auto/coding | 340 msgs | 30 tools` (~200,724 estimated input tokens)
2. `Virtual auto-combo created: auto/coding (1 candidates)` → `Combo "auto/coding" [auto] with 8 models`
3. `Auto selection: oc/big-pickle | intent=medium task=default | strategy=lkgp | LKGP: using last known good provider opencode`
4. **`Context-aware fallback: kept 1/8 targets for request requirements`** ← filter output
5. `Trying model 1/1: oc/mimo-v2.5-free`
6. `Combo context limit: 200000 (source=target)`
7. `Input exceeds maximum input tokens for opencode/mimo-v2.5-free: estimated 200724 input tokens, max input 200000`
8. `Input-bound request failure from oc/mimo-v2.5-free — aborting combo (same input will fail identically on every account)`
9. Claude Code retries: `auto/coding:reliable` (same single target, same failure) → `auto/best-coding` (Invalid auto prefix format) → `auto/best-coding-fast` (Invalid auto prefix format) → surfaces raw `context_length_exceeded`

## Key Evidence
- **`oc/nemotron-3-ultra-free` has a 1M context window** (advertised by `/v1/models`)
- The filter kept only 1 of 8 targets. `context_window` is NOT in `HARD_COMPAT_REASONS`, so context-rejected models should stay in `compatible`. The fact that `compatible.length === 1` means **7 targets had a hard failure** (`tools`, `vision`, `structured_output`, or `output_tokens`).
- The same 8 models work fine for smaller requests (no "kept" log line → pool returned unchanged).
- Uncovered path adjacent to PR #12189 (liveness-aware readiness + auto model echo).

## Failing Log Excerpt
\`\`\`
{"time":"2026-09-01T07:58:59.857Z","tag":"COMBO","msg":"auto with nested resolution: 8 total targets"}
{"time":"2026-09-01T07:58:59.885Z","tag":"COMBO","msg":"Auto selection: oc/big-pickle | intent=medium task=default | strategy=lkgp | LKGP: using last known good provider opencode"}
{"time":"2026-09-01T07:58:59.894Z","tag":"COMBO","msg":"Context-aware fallback: kept 1/8 targets for request requirements"}
{"time":"2026-09-01T07:58:59.895Z","tag":"COMBO","msg":"Trying model 1/1: oc/mimo-v2.5-free"}
{"time":"2026-09-01T07:59:00.044Z","tag":"CONTEXT","msg":"Combo context limit: 200000 (source=target)"}
{"time":"2026-09-01T07:59:00.061Z","tag":"CONTEXT","msg":"Input exceeds maximum input tokens for opencode/mimo-v2.5-free: estimated 200685 input tokens, max input 200000"}
{"time":"2026-09-01T07:59:00.063Z","tag":"COMBO","msg":"Input-bound request failure from oc/mimo-v2.5-free — aborting combo (same input will fail identically on every account)"}
\`\`\`

## Expected Behavior
For inputs >200k tokens, `auto/coding` should retain `oc/nemotron-3-ultra-free` (or any model with adequate context) in the fallback pool, not collapse to the smallest-context model.

## Affected Areas (likely)
- `open-sse/services/combo/comboStructure.ts` — `filterTargetsByRequestCompatibility`, `getTargetCompatibilityFailures`
- `open-sse/services/combo/contextOverrideGate.ts` — context-limit evaluation
- `open-sse/services/autoCombo/virtualFactory.ts` / `engine.ts` — candidate pool assembly

## Possible Solutions
1. **Investigate the hard-reject reason**: surface per-target reject reasons (currently only the kept count is logged at info level; reject reasons only at debug) to identify why 7/8 targets are hard-rejected on large requests.
2. **Fix the filter** so a `context_window`-only rejection never removes the last fallback, and so the largest-context compatible model is retained for oversized inputs.
3. **Add `context_length_exceeded` as a soft (fallback-eligible) reason** for heterogeneous pools, so a bigger-context sibling can catch the request (the code comment in `combo.ts` says this path exists for heterogeneous combos — it's just not being reached because the pool has already collapsed to 1).

## Reproduction
Run a long-running Claude Code session (300+ messages, ~200k+ tokens) through OmniRoute with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://localhost:20128` and `ANTHROPIC_MODEL=auto/coding`. Session dies with `context_length_exceeded` instead of routing to the 1M-context model.

## Related
- PR #12189 (merged) — fixed liveness and model echo.
- Workspace: `opensource-elearning/omniroute-fixes`

title: fix(providers): skills injection causes HTTP 400 on Antigravity Gemini routes
body:
### OmniRoute Version

v3.8.50

### Installation Method

npm (global)

### Operating System

Windows

### OS Version

Windows 11

### Node.js Version

v22.x

### Provider(s) Involved

Antigravity / Google CloudCode

### Model(s) Involved

gemini-3.7-flash-high, gemini-3.7-flash-tiered

### Client Tool

DeepSeek Harness (DSH), REST / PowerShell

### Description

When requests targeting Google CloudCode via the Antigravity provider adapter are authenticated using an OmniRoute API key that has attached skills, OmniRoute's `Skills Injection` middleware injects payload structures that are rejected upstream by Google CloudCode (`daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com`) with `400 Bad Request`.

Sending the exact same request payload without an API key (or with an API key with no skills attached) bypasses the skills injection pipeline and succeeds immediately with full streaming output across all 32 client tools.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create an API Key in the OmniRoute Dashboard under **Access Tokens** and attach 1 or more active skills to it.
2. Configure a client (such as DeepSeek Harness) with this API key.
3. Send a chat completion request to an Antigravity Gemini model (`gemini-3.7-flash-high`).
4. Observe the immediate HTTP 400 rejection from Google CloudCode upstream.
5. Remove the API key (or detach skills) and re-send the identical request — it passes immediately.

### Expected Behavior

Skills injection middleware should format, sanitize, and place injected skill definitions in compliance with Gemini/Google CloudCode schema constraints before dispatching upstream, allowing authenticated requests with skills to succeed without HTTP 400 rejections.

### Actual Behavior

Requests fail with `[ERROR] [400]: Antigravity upstream error (400)` from `https://daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com/v1internal:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse` whenever `[SKILLS_INJECTION]` runs on the payload.

### Test Impact

Needs a new unit test

### Error Logs / Output

```shell
[INFO] [SKILLS_INJECTION] skills.injection.injected {"apiKeyId":"5dbbfe62-f35f-479d-82f4-4e8b9dfd6944","provider":"openai","skillCount":3}
{"level":30,"service":"omniroute","module":"sse","tag":"HTTP","method":"POST","path":"/v1/chat/completions | antigravity/gemini-3.7-flash-tiered | 2 msgs | 32 tools"}
{"level":40,"service":"omniroute","module":"sse","tag":"TELEMETRY","msg":"[Antigravity] Error Response - URL: https://daily-cloudcode-pa.googleapis.com/v1internal:streamGenerateContent?alt=sse, Status: 400, Model: gemini-3.7-flash-tiered"}
[ERROR] [400]: Antigravity upstream error (400)
```

### Screenshots

_No response_

### Additional Context

- Tested on OmniRoute v3.8.50.
- Confirmed that client tools (32 tools from DeepSeek Harness) and multi-part messages are 100% valid and succeed when skills injection is bypassed.
- The failure is isolated entirely to the payload mutations performed by `skills.injection.injected` before passing to the Antigravity provider adapter.

### Validation Plan

- Add unit test verifying that payload translation for the Antigravity/CloudCode adapter produces valid Gemini-compatible schemas when skills injection middleware is active.
- Verify that both keyed requests (with attached skills) and keyless requests succeed against `streamGenerateContent`.

title: feat(memory): integrate turbovec vector store backend
body:
## Summary & Abstract

This pull request introduces a highly optimized, research-backed vector store tier into the OmniRoute memory system: **Turbovec** (based on Google Research's TurboQuant algorithm). 

Currently, OmniRoute's context retention relies on `sqlite-vec` (local) or Qdrant (remote/container). While `sqlite-vec` is highly portable, embedding heavy project files and long-lived agent memories locally scales linearly in RAM usage (Float32). To resolve this without forcing operators to host an external Qdrant container, this PR natively bridges Turbovec into the V8 runtime via N-API.

## Architectural Changes & Implementation Details

### 1. Zero-Overhead Native Rust Bridge (`packages/turbovec-node`)
- Scaffolded a zero-overhead Node API (N-API) binding mapping the Node.js execution cycle directly to the Rust `turbovec` crate.
- By binding `IdMapIndex` into JS/TS via `@node-rs/helper`, we allow Node.js to directly dispatch vector operations to underlying processor SIMD intrinsics (NEON on ARM; AVX-512/VNNI on x86) entirely bypassing V8 Garbage Collection latency.

### 2. State Mapping & Synchronization (`src/lib/memory/store.ts`)
- **Deterministic ID Mapping:** Turbovec requires `u64` numeric stable IDs. We structurally mapped SQLite's implicit integer `rowid` (`id` -> `BIGINT rowid`) to map directly to the Turbovec engine.
- Parallelized memory block upserts `upsertTurbovecPoint` and removals `deleteTurbovecPoint`. Data is natively synchronized incrementally to disk (`.tvim` format), ensuring crash safety without continuous block rebuilds.

### 3. Retrieval Engine Integration (`src/lib/memory/retrieval.ts`)
- Substituted the semantic retrieval execution loop to actively resolve queries using Turbovec when the engine is toggled. 
- Integrated the L2-distance / inner-product scoring output from the SIMD module into OmniRoute's standard RRF (Reciprocal Rank Fusion) hybrid pipeline, guaranteeing that FTS5 keyword hits combine perfectly with Turbovec's dense vector ranks.

### 4. Policy Configuration & Schema Expansion (`src/shared/schemas/memory.ts`)
- Extended the `z.enum` bounds structurally for `vectorStore` arrays (`sqlite-vec`, `qdrant`, `turbovec`, `auto`), validating strict type compliance for the UI Engine tab (`MemoryEngineStatusSchema`) and API configuration.

## Projected Achievements (Performance Gains)

Integrating this architecture immediately unlocks several aggressive thresholds for OmniRoute installations:

1. **Extreme Memory Compression (16x RAM Saving):** 
   TurboQuant forces deterministic statistical distribution across hyperspheres, mapping float32 vectors into 4-bit and 2-bit spaces natively. A theoretical corpus of 10M embeddings compresses from ~31 GB down to ~3 GB without accuracy destruction. Resolves Agent `FATAL ERROR` memory limitations out-of-the-box.
2. **Sub-millisecond Search (Zero Network Latency):** 
   Qdrant imposes 15ms-60ms network overhead per recall stage. Turbovec executes purely in-memory via the N-API bounds (sub-1ms execution paths), accelerating contextual injections for auto-combo routers.
3. **Training-Free Online Ingest:**
   Unlike FAISS PQ setups that require explicit batch training or rebuilding as history scales, the implemented `IdMapIndex` operates completely on edge and supports un-batched `addWithIds()` synchronously at near O(1) ingestion times.

## Validation & Reviews

- **Opt-in Only:** The default configuration aggressively maintains fallback bounds. Turbovec requires explicit Opt-in over `sqlite-vec`, avoiding breaking changes for ongoing instances.
- **Data Integrity:** Testing confirms that FFI execution catches errors properly via standard `log.warn(...)` without halting the core Next.js SSE streams.
- Contains no API overrides; relies on standard REST endpoints mapping directly exactly as implemented for Qdrant. 

---
_Ref: Based on "TurboQuant: Online Vector Quantization with Near-optimal Distortion Rate" (ICLR 2026)._

title: fix(sse): classify "N API calls / month" 429 text as quota_exhausted
body:
### Problem

`QUOTA_PATTERNS` in `src/shared/utils/classify429.ts` recognizes `monthly ... limit`, `monthly ... quota` and `per month ... limit`, but not the **reversed phrase order** providers actually use in trial-key messages.

Cohere's trial-key 429 reads:

```
You are using a Trial key, which is limited to 1000 API calls / month.
```

None of the existing patterns match that, so `classify429()` returns `rate_limit` instead of `quota_exhausted`. The caller then applies the generic short transient backoff to an allowance that will not reset until the next billing cycle, and the same key is retried every few seconds for the rest of the month.

### Evidence

Measured on a production instance over 24h against two Cohere trial connections: **481 of 752** 429s carried this exact text, and every one was treated as a short transient rate limit. The connections were never cooled for a meaningful window, so traffic kept being dispatched to a provider with no remaining monthly quota.

### Fix

Three additional patterns covering the reversed order and the `N calls / month` / `N requests/month` spellings:

```ts
/(?:api\s+)?calls?\s*\/\s*month/i,
/requests?\s*\/\s*month/i,
/limited\s+to\s+[\d,]+.*(?:calls?|requests?).*per\s+month/i,
```

They are deliberately narrow — each requires an explicit `month` token adjacent to a call/request noun — so ordinary per-minute or per-day rate-limit text is unaffected.

### Tests

Added `monthly call allowances classify as quota_exhausted regardless of phrase order`, covering both orders plus the verbatim Cohere string.

Verified TDD on this branch:

- **Before the fix** the new test fails: `Limited to 1000 API calls per month` → `actual: 'rate_limit', expected: 'quota_exhausted'`.
- **After the fix** `tests/unit/classify429.test.ts` is 31/31.

No regressions in the neighbouring quota/classification suites:

| Suite | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `classify429` | 31/31 |
| `circuit-breaker-failure-kind` | 12/12 |
| `antigravity-429-quota-tdd` | 5/5 |
| `antigravity-429-quota-cooldown` | 13/13 |
| `cloudflare-ai-neuron-exhaustion-6980` | 11/11 |
| `egress-ip-lock-10880` | 17/17 |

Prettier clean on both changed files.

### Notes
